articles.title: Canva despedirá a 1.271 empleados, el 22% de su plantilla, pero la IA no los remplazará
articles.text:
Canva, la empresa australiana de diseño gráfico usada por cientos de millones de personas, afectará a 1.271 trabajadores, el 22% de su plantilla, con una reestructuración anunciada el 4 de noviembre. La compañía aseguró que no usará inteligencia artificial para hacer el trabajo de quienes se vayan.
La cifra incluye despidos, cambios de funciones y traslados a Sídney, y la empresa no precisó cuántas personas perderán el empleo. Lo informó la directora ejecutiva y cofundadora, Melanie Perkins, en un correo a los empleados que Canva publicó luego en su sala de prensa.
Perkins calificó el momento como el más difícil en los 13 años de historia de la empresa. Escribió que el crecimiento se desaceleró este año por primera vez en una década y que cambios menores no bastaban para “refundar” Canva.
Qué cambia dentro de la empresa
La carta describe tres medidas: unir las áreas de producto, crecimiento y plataforma en una sola organización, reducir las especialidades estrechas para crear puestos más amplios y concentrar equipos en centros comunes. Sídney será la sede principal de más equipos de producto.
A partir de enero, la mayoría de los empleados con modalidad híbrida deberá ir a la oficina entre dos y tres días por semana, según el texto de Perkins.
Quienes pierdan el puesto recibirán al menos seis meses de salario, doce meses de cobertura de salud donde la empresa la ofrece y la posibilidad de quedarse con su computadora portátil. También habrá becas de USD 10.000 para quienes quieran emprender; tienen hasta el 14 de diciembre para inscribirse.
El debate sobre el papel de la IA
La carta habla de nueva tecnología que transforma lo que la gente crea y espera, pero no menciona la inteligencia artificial. Consultada por la agencia australiana AAP, la empresa respondió que la IA cambia los productos que construye, pero que los roles de las personas que se van no pasarán a ser hechos por IA.
Un vocero de Canva dijo a AAP: “Estos cambios buscan preparar a Canva para construir esos productos, no usar IA para hacer el trabajo de las personas que se van”.
El sindicato Professionals Australia pidió más claridad. Su director para el sector tecnológico, Paul Inglis, afirmó que las grandes empresas del rubro deben ser honestas sobre el efecto de la IA en el empleo. Después señaló que Atlassian y WiseTech Global reconocieron el papel de esa tecnología en sus recortes, y que “es difícil entender la magnitud de los despidos si no es por la IA”, según el Daily Mail.
AAP recordó que Atlassian redujo en marzo su plantilla en 1.600 personas, y que WiseTech Global anunció recortes de hasta 2.000 puestos, luego revisados a 1.700. Ambas atribuyeron los cambios a la IA.
Un negocio presionado por la IA
TechCrunch informó que Canva recortó su pronóstico de crecimiento de ingresos de 30% a 20% por el aumento de los costos de sus funciones de IA, y que sus primeros inversores redujeron su valuación a unos USD 35.000 millones este año. Adam Barty, director de la consultora Revium, dijo a AAP que “es difícil no ver la IA como una amenaza existencial” para el modelo de negocio de Canva.
Tres semanas después, el Daily Mail publicó que fuentes anónimas aseguran que hubo salidas silenciosas en los meses previos y que la cifra real de personas que dejaron la empresa este año es mayor. Canva respondió que la gestión del desempeño es independiente de la reestructuración y que no hay metas de despidos por rendimiento.
Canva no detalló qué funciones ni qué países concentrarán los recortes. Storyboard18 informó que el área de contenido para India figura entre los equipos alcanzados, aunque la empresa no dio cifras locales.

articles.title: Notée 5/5, cette souris Logitech passe à 139,99 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La souris Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike "5 étoiles" à 139,99 € (-11%)
Actuellement notée 5/5 par notre rédaction, la Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike se distingue par des clics analogiques haptiques personnalisables et une réactivité exemplaire pour le jeu. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre son prix à 139,99 € chez Boulanger.com et Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 11 % et 16,46 € d'économie.
La Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike est une souris pour joueurs qui intègre des clics analogiques haptiques. Le fabricant remplace ici les commutateurs optiques habituels par un capteur à induction pour optimiser la réactivité en jeu. Ce modèle sans fil avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage aux tests.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike descend à 139,99 € chez Boulanger.com et Amazon, soit environ 11 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (156,45 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 16,46 € sur ce périphérique.
Des déclencheurs analogiques haptiques pour une réactivité maximale
Avec ce modèle actuellement noté 5/5, la marque suisse intègre un système de clics analogiques inédit couplé à un capteur optique montant jusqu'à 44 000 dpi. Ce dispositif permet de personnaliser entièrement la sensibilité du déclenchement tout en assurant une frappe rapide et silencieuse. Comme le souligne notre test complet, la souris s'appuie également sur une vitesse de transmission sans fil montant à 8 000 Hz via son dongle USB pour retranscrire immédiatement les mouvements les plus vifs.
Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike
Points forts
- Design sobre et intéressant…
- Prise en main presque universelle.
- Légère.
- Clics personnalisables à l'envi.
- Rapidité des déclencheurs analogiques.
- Silencieuse en toutes circonstances.
Points faibles
- …à une faute de goût près.
- Connectivité 2,4 GHz uniquement.
- Pas de bouton DPI.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une prise en main fluide malgré quelques limites d'équipement
Le châssis profite d'une prise en main presque universelle qui convient à la majorité des morphologies. La souris se limite toutefois à une liaison sans fil 2,4 GHz exclusive et ne dispose d'aucun bouton dédié au changement de sensibilité sous les doigts, ce qui ne posera aucun souci aux joueurs qui règlent définitivement leur profil en amont.
Logitech G502 X Plus : l'autre option face au Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike
La Logitech G502 X Plus adopte une orientation différente avec sa molette débrayable et ses commandes plus nombreuses, là où la Pro X2 Superstrike vise l'efficacité brute avec 5 boutons et ses contacteurs analogiques haptiques. Les deux modèles partagent une note actuelle de 5/5, mais la G502 X Plus s'affiche à 79,99 €, soit 60,00 € de moins que la Pro X2 Superstrike à son tarif du jour.
La Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike conserve l'avantage de ses clics analogiques haptiques pour le jeu compétitif, mais la Logitech G502 X Plus reste bien plus accessible grâce à son tarif inférieur de 60,00 €.
Logitech G502 X Plus
Points forts
- Qualité de construction.
- Polyvalence gaming et bureautique.
- Nombreux boutons paramétrables.
- Molette inclinable et débrayable.
- Capteur très précis.
- Rétroéclairage bien intégré.
- Bouton "sniper" modulaire.
Points faibles
- Pas de version pour gauchers.
- Pas de Bluetooth.
- Un peu lourde pour du FPS.

articles.title: I put the best headphones from Apple, Technics, Bowers & Wilkins and Nothing in group test to find my ultimate winner — and the result may surprise you
articles.text:
I tested four of the best wireless noise-canceling headphones in 2026, and there's only one pair I’d buy on Black Friday
Four of 2026's best wireless headphones, tested side by side to find a winner
It has been an absolute barnstormer year for over-ear headphones. I’ve personally reviewed several of the best noise-canceling headphones of 2026 — and I even put two of them head-to-head in my Apple AirPods Max 2 vs. Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 showdown, a few months after the AirPods' March release.
Now, (and with Black Friday around the corner; see those early Black Friday deals landing as I type, like apples from a tree) I think we need to extend the group test to include four key models you're likely to see discounts on this peak sales season.
Fortunately, I reviewed (or, in two cases, helped test) all four sets of headphones, and I've got them here in front of me now for a group showdown.
Under direct comparison, I'm going to tell you which feels best on, looks best, sounds the most faithfully detailed, lasts the longest, and is the easiest to use — because maybe you're buying for someone not quite so tech-savvy, and giving them a gift they'll love using is a perfectly valid, kind concern (so well done on that).
All four models earned glowing 5-star or 4.5-star ratings under TechRadar's rigorous review process, so they're all very good indeed. A part of me knows that whichever you pick, you won't be disappointed. Then again, my modus operandi as TechRadar's Audio Editor is getting you the ideal set of cans for you or whomever you're buying for.
So let's work out which of this quartet of cans that is, shall we? Meet the players: 
Apple AirPods Max 2; unveiled March 16, 2026 — $549 / £499 / AU$999
Technics EAH-A1000; unveiled September 29, 2026 — $449 / £399 / AU$699
Nothing Headphone (a); unveiled March 13, 2026 — $199 / £149 / AU$329
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2; unveiled September 24, 2025 — $799 / £629 / AU$1,299
Now, let's go…
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Design, comfort and battery life
We're not messing around here — time is of the essence. The easiest thing is to list the cans, with their perks and shortfalls, succinctly and directly. So here it is folks…
Apple AirPods Max 2
The good: without a doubt, the most comfortable of the quartet — despite being the heaviest, at 386.2g. The mesh headband may look a little bizarre, but it distributes weight beautifully across the crown of the head and, as someone who experiences migraines complete with auras (don't even get me started), comfort is an important thing to note. Another highlight is the Digital Crown volume roller on the top right earcup. Clamping force is gentle but effective, and the ear cups, while big, are relatively nice and close to the ear. 
The bad: you only get up to 20 hours of stamina (with ANC enabled), which is the worst battery life in this roundup. Also, that case is possibly the flimsiest and easiest to lose of the lot.
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2
The good: emphatically the most winsome and elite-looking of the bunch and yes, they're also comfortable. There’s just the right amount of memory foam beneath the headband (which is also renewable or replaceable, by a qualified technician — a nice touch given the considerable asking fee). Despite the ample sprinkling of burnished aluminum and even a flourish of exposed cable detail on the yokes, they weigh just 310g too. Unlike AirPods above, you get aptX Adaptive and aptX Lossless codec support, if you're an Android owner with access to music files of quality. 
The bad: battery life is a little better than the AirPods Max at 30 hours with ANC on, but it's far from the best here. The build also features Nappa leather, so they're no good for vegetarians. The hard-shell case feels premium, but can feel a tad large because these cans lie flat but do not fold.
Nothing Headphone (a)
The good: given that they're by far the cheapest in this group test, at $199 / £149 / AU$329, there's an awful lot to love about the build quality, which weighs 310g (like the B&W above) and, like the above two models, also supports USB-C wired audio. Unlike the two picks above, you get LDAC support here (great for Sony and Samsung handset owners), and the on-ear controls have no business being this good at this level. In particular, the roller for volume control is exceptional and makes other solutions feel crude by comparison. Then, there's the 'rocker' control underneath, which is also beautifully intuitive for track skips. Top it off with a round multi-function custom button and if it's easy-to-use you want, these are the cans. Oh, and I haven't mentioned stamina! At up to 135 hours, it's superb. OK, that's with ANC off, but still, we're looking at class-leading here. 
The bad: these aren't cans for the clumsy: you only get a flimsy pouch to put them in, which doesn't bode well for bag slingers.
Technics EAH-A1000
The good: the lightest in the roundup, at 306g, but they never ever look or feel flimsy — and comfort levels are spot on. Also, the 'leather' is vegan, which is a big tick for those who only support vegan products. These headphones are understatedly elegant and, with up to 45 hours with ANC on or up to 90 hours with ANC off, they're on the money there too. While the ear cups do protrude a fair way, the 18-degree angle was particularly comfortable for me, a woman — and indeed, the design engineer here is a woman, so depending on whom you're buying these for, worth considering. Again, there's USB-C wired audio support, and Technics' magnetic fluid driver tech is a first in this over-ear category. The case? It's hard-shell, bijou, and quite beautiful.
The bad: the downside here is the on-ear controls. They're physical buttons, and while acceptable in use, they do occasionally fail to register presses. In direct comparison to others in this roundup, they're not as reliable for playback, volume handling, and powering off.
- Design/aesthetics winner: Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2
- Comfort winner: Apple AirPods Max 2
- Stamina winner: Nothing Headphone (a)
Features and ANC
Apple AirPods Max 2
The good: if you have an iPhone, the ANC here is unmatched. Apple has made these headphones ideal for the iOS ensconced — and to that end, if you've got a newer iPhone with Apple Intelligence, you get Live Translation. You can deploy it easily, via the Digital Crown and it is exceptional for travellers. Also exceptional is Apple's Spatial Audio with head-tracking, and if you don't believe me, grab an iPad and stream the movie Gravity using Apple's head-tracked spatial side-sauce. See? Also, the Conversation Awareness perk (pipe up and the music pipes down and transparency kicks in, so you'll hear whatever was just said to you) is a winner all day long. 
The bad: Don't have an iPhone? You'll need to move on I fear — you really aren't getting them at their best with an Android phone. Also perhaps worth noting is that even with an iPhone, you won't get Apple's earbuds-only heart-rate monitoring or hearing tests to generate the Cupertino giant's hearing-aid-like features.
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2: 
The good: these headphones are not overly stuffed with extraneous features (no live translation, hearing tests or gesture support here) but what they do, they do well — and there's beauty in the detail. The Wear Sensing feature, for example, makes for a truly natural headphone experience, pausing and resuming your music simply by lifting either earpiece on or off your ear. It sounds simple but when it works this well, you'll never want cans without it.
The bad: the ANC here is fine, rather than fantastic — and while they shine in other areas, at this price we are allowed to be a little pickier. Also, True Immersion (B&W's spatial audio offering) is acceptable, rather than truly awesome.
Nothing Headphone (a) 
The good: for the money, the ANC is spot on. It's not AirPods Max 2 good, but that's hardly fair given they're less than half the price of those. What you will get is a few fun device-agnostic ways to enhance the sound, including an AI Dynamic Bass Enhancement option, plus two device-neutral Spatial Audio modes (Concert or Cinema) to enhance your source material. Neither option includes dynamic head tracking but they still add depth and value to the proposition. 
The bad: there's no auto-pause feature (also called wearer detection) to halt playback when you take them off. It's a shame — it's relatively standard even in affordable cans now.
Technics EAH-A1000
The good: there's wearer detection to pause your music, plus ANC that can either be set to 'Adaptive', to automatically adjust, or simply 'On' to tweak manually as you move to busier environments. This is done on a little virtual dial within the easy-to-navigate (and easy-to-tailor) Technics AudioConnect app. For me, dialling up the ANC to 100% or thereabouts gives very good results — better than the B&W and Nothing options, if not quite as good as AirPods. Also competent is the spatial audio offering, which can be deployed head-tracking. It's a more subtle effect than with AirPods Max but still, it absolutely deserves merit. 
The bad: you'll get no hearing tests, hearing aid perks or scope for nodding to summon your voice assistant here and while I perhaps don't miss these features, it's my job to note their absence. Also, the Transparency profile felt a little undercooked — I could use more help to hear external sounds.
- Features winner: 
iOS — Apple AirPods Max 2
Android — Nothing Headphone (a)
- ANC winner: 
iOS — AirPods Max 2
Android — Technics EAH A1000
Sound quality
Apple AirPods Max 2: expect an expansive, unfurled sound with bass frequencies that rumble, snap and boom. Timing, too, is exceptional. I dare you to stream Bad Bunny's Tití Me Preguntó and not dance.
For crisp leading edges of notes and an extra ounce of detail, you'll get just a touch more insight and loyalty to the original recording from the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2, but AirPods Max 2's Spatial Audio beats B&W's True Immersion, with the latter coming off a little veiled in direct comparison. This is a fun, zealous, expansive listen and no mistake.
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2: if you buy these headphones, let it be for their detailed, faithful, neutral, critical sound quality, dear reader. Turning all ANC and extras off, it’s hard to lay a glove on the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 in this key area. Where they really excel, they leave their nominal competition for dust. The size and coherence of the soundstage they create is class-leading; the dynamic nuance is like the hand of a skilled surgeon; the forensic level of insight is nothing short of superb. If it’s scale, variation and detail you want from your headphones, you've just found your ideal set — if your budget can stretch to them.
Nothing Headphone (a) 
The spaciousness here runs rings around Nothing's inaugural July 2025-issue Headphone (1) although I know that comparison isn't why we're here. The midrange expresses itself beautifully, but the treble never feels like it's pushing to compete in the mix. If anything, the opposite is true: there is a marginal softness of detail or roundness to the Headphone (a)'s sound. Don't get me wrong, they are not poor for the money, but if your budget stretches further, better sound can be had higher up the food chain. Switch to any other headphone in this roundup and crisper leading edges of notes can be yours. I know, it stands to reason that an expensive thing will sound better than a cheaper thing (and lo! It has come to pass) but still, it's my job to point that out. 
Technics EAH-A1000
If you need exceptionally detailed audio, with expanse and no musical passage left behind, overshadowed or ignored, these are your headphones. For lovers of an integrated, neutral hi-fi sound in headphones that can be used to dig out extra sonic surprises in their higher-resolution music files, these headphones won't disappoint. But there's a downside: they also very occasionally come off a little too polite and lacking in bite and excitement — it's marginal, but it's there. Nothing in Technics' headphones is ever over-emphasised or bloated, but in making sure they never offend, sometimes they're a little too mild-mannered for my listening taste. 
- Sound quality winner: Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2
The overall winner (as Black Friday approaches, fast)
Oh it's a tough one, isn't it? In fact, I cannot give you a one product answer, since these cans are all the best — in certain areas.
But while I can't give you a simple "it's these, no question" answer, I can give you concrete answers. My succinct-as-I-can-make-it verdict is this: for stonkingly good sound above all else, you need to be going for the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2.
If ANC and/or Spatial Audio performance is your top priority, it's got to be the AirPods Max 2 — provided you've got an iPhone (if not, allow me to nudge you towards the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones Gen 2, for similar money).
For detailed neutrality and a superbly chic, comfortable, beautiful design (especially for a female wearer; perhaps one who adores classical or acoustic music) look to the Technics EAH-A1000.
And if battery-life is at the very top of your checklist, do not overlook the Nothing Headphone (a) — because this is the set that will still be playing long after the other three headphones in this list have had to go for a charge…

Becky became Audio Editor at TechRadar in 2024, but joined the team in 2022 as Senior Staff Writer, focusing on all things hi-fi. Before this, she spent three years at What Hi-Fi? testing and reviewing everything from wallet-friendly wireless earbuds to huge high-end sound systems. Prior to gaining her MA in Journalism in 2018, Becky freelanced as an arts critic alongside a 22-year career as a professional dancer and aerialist – any love of dance starts with a love of music. articles.title: GTA 6 établit un record absolu de ventes mondiales durant les 24 premières heures !
articles.text:
C'est une fin de semaine historique dans le monde des jeux vidéos. Car GTA 6 a affiché des chiffres de ventes faramineux durant ces 24 premières heures !
Impossible de passer à côté, tant on a l'impression que l'on n'a parlé que de ça durant toute la semaine ! GTA 6 est en effet enfin sorti le 19 novembre dernier, avec une attente si forte que les opérateurs des télécommunications ont dû muscler leurs réseaux pour être sûrs de pouvoir continuer à fonctionner correctement malgré l'afflux de téléchargements. Et ça n'était pas une prévention inutile quand on voit ces chiffres !
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
3,79 milliards de dollars de ventes en 24 heures après le lancement pour GTA 6
Oui, on le sait, GTA 6 est très attendu, et a dû compter de très nombreux clients dès les premières minutes de son lancement. Mais tout de même, les chiffres de ventes sont fabuleux, et historiques.
RockStar a ainsi enregistré 3,79 milliards de dollars de ventes durant les 24 heures qui sont suivi le lancement de GTA 6. Un chiffre qui établit un record mondial pour ce nouvel opus de Grand Theft Auto, non seulement dans le secteur du jeu vidéo, mais aussi plus largement dans le domaine du divertissement.
Un lancement cinq fois plus puissant que celui de GTA 5 !
En 24 heures, Rockstar a ainsi fait mieux que le film Avengers : Endgame, qui est le film ayant généré le plus de recettes dans l'histoire (à savoir 2,942 milliards de dollars). Et si l'on doit évidemment relativiser la comparaison, un jeu vidéo n'étant pas un film, on peut rappeler que Rockstar a établi ces chiffres en 24 heures, contrairement au film Marvel.
Autre point de comparaison, pour situer la performance, on peut noter que GTA 6 a fait un début infiniment plus puissant que son précédesseur, GTA 5. Celui-ci avait en effet réussi à générer à sa sortie en 2013 près de 800 millions de dollars de vente dans les 24 premières heures, ce qui était à l'époque déjà un record pour l'industrie du jeu vidéo. GTA 6 a ainsi fait 5 fois mieux !
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Vuelve a tiendas Lidl el sábado 28 (por 100 euros menos) el robot de cocina superventas Monsieur Cuisine con pantalla táctil, báscula y más
articles.text:
Aún no ha llegado el Black Friday como tal, que tendrá lugar el próximo viernes 27 de noviembre, pero muchas tiendas están ya inmersas en sus campañas de rebajas desde hace días. Una de ellas es Lidl, que en su último folleto (centrado en el Black Friday) ha anunciado las rebajas de muchos de sus productos estrella y las fechas en que llegarán. Y han dejado para el final el bombazo: su robot de cocina superventas costará 399,99 euros.
Ufesa TotalChef RK7
Dicho robot ya se puede conseguir en Lidl online, a su PVP de 499,99 euros eso sí. O por 100 euros menos en tiendas Lidl en apenas unos días. Pero si no conseguimos hincarle el diente ni de una forma ni de otra, en Amazon encontramos una estupenda alternativa, incluso más barata por Black Friday: el TotalChef de Ufesa, rebajado a 319,99 euros.
Un robot para todo tipo de elaboraciones: postres, guisos, salsas...
Concretamente, es el próximo sábado 28 de noviembre (la jornada tras el Black Friday) cuando regresa a tiendas Lidl el Monsieur Cuisine Smart rebajado. Lo hará junto a su versión Compact, que tendrá un precio (también rebajado) de 149,99 euros. Aunque viendo que este último ya se encuentra agotado online a su PVP, es lógico pensar que ambos robots se agotarán rápidamente.
Si llegamos a tiempo, con el Monsieur Cuisine Smart nos llevamos a casa una estupenda alternativa económica a robots de cocina mucho más caros, como algunos modelos de Thermomix que incluso superan los 1.500 euros. Un dispositivo versátil como pocos con el que preparar toda clase de platos.
El Monsieur Cuisine Smart tiene una potencia de 1.200 W, una capacidad de 4,5 litros y 10 niveles de velocidad. Con multitud de programas automáticos con los que cocinar al vapor, sofreír, realizar cocciones lentas, al vacío, amasar e incluso fermentar. Todo ello, con una balanza integrada y una pantalla táctil que facilita mucho el cocinado.
Además, se incluye una aplicación gratuita con más de 1.000 recetas paso a paso. Con planificación semanal, vídeos y la posibilidad de añadir directamente a la lista de la compra los ingredientes necesarios para muchas de ellas. En conjunto, un robot de cocina completísimo para lo que cuesta, perfecto para hacer guisos, salsas, postres y mucho más.

articles.title: Xiaomi Clip review: simply the best open earbuds you can buy, and I've tested scores of them
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Of all the open earbuds on the market, the Xiaomi Clip are the best so far — and I say that as someone who's tested virtually every set of this design to have crossed TechRadar's desk in the past two years. They sound great, fit reliably, and come in a tiny carry case. Best of all, they're not prohibitively expensive, undercutting several premium options. The only thing that stops them getting a perfect, five-star review is the lack of an equalizer or support for LDAC.
Reasons to buy
- + Energetic sound
- + Tiny carry case
- + Reliable, secure fit
Reasons to avoid
- - No equalizer tab
- - Lacking support for LDAC
- - Some may call them gaudy(?)
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Xiaomi Clip: Two-minute review
During the years I've spent testing the best open earbuds, I've patiently been waiting for that one 'wow' model — the set I use as a default when I've got nothing to test; the pair I can leap to when someone asks which model they should buy. Well, finally, I can say I've found that product.
The Xiaomi Clip come from a pretty unsuspecting company, given that the Xiaomi OpenWear Stereo Pro were the second-worst open earbuds I've tested. Clearly the company's learnt from its mistakes, though, because its debut cuff-style buds are a winner.
Clipping (or ear cuff-style, if you prefer) earbuds like these don't have much scope for variety. And Xiaomi wins here not by launching some surprising spec or trait unavailable in rivals, but simply by ticking all the boxes and not presenting any major issues.
The Xiaomi Clip fit well, locking into your ear without wobbling or falling out, and I spent hours running and cycling with them during the testing process with no design issue uncovered. I love the carry case too, because it's tiny and feels premium.
While open earbuds will never sound truly fantastic to an audiophile (given that wired IEMs exist), the Xiaomi Clip are amongst the best I've heard; they offer the simple but solid V-shaped sound that fitness buyers generally prefer. They're detailed and hearty, even if you can't tweak the sound yourself.
In terms of features, they tick most (though not all) of the usual boxes, but don't excel as much as in other areas; the battery life and app offerings are all what you'd expect. The exception is a recording feature, which a few audio brands are starting to offer, letting you record voice memos or conversations using the case or buds.
When I first started testing the Xiaomi Clip, I wasn't told the price, and made a few mental guesses about the eventual cost. I was wrong — they're cheaper than I expected. So, these are in fact relatively affordable mid-range open earbuds that match Bose and Shokz' budget offerings.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I spent most of the review process sure that these would be five-star buds, but I decided to dock a half-star at the eleventh hour due to some missing features. The buds don't support LDAC and nor do they have an equalizer. The first is a shame but I can overlook it, however the latter will be a problem for a lot of listeners. Hey, Xiaomi: if you make a follow-up bud, you know what you need to do to get that perfect score.
I've used the Xiaomi Clip for several weeks, and I know they'll continue to be my go-to open earbuds for the foreseeable future. They're the best clipping buds so far, and one to beat for all other brands in this highly competitive area. If you're on the market for an option, it's easy for me to recommend them.
Xiaomi Clip: Price and release date
- Released in November in Europe and Australia
- Sells for £129.99 / AU$199 (about $160)
- Not on sale in the US
The Xiaomi Clip were unveiled on November 17, 2026, alongside some new wearables from the company as well as the Xiaomi 18 Pro smartphone series. That’s a little over a year on from the release of its first open earbuds.
You can buy the buds for £129.99 / AU$199 so they’re mid-priced options which undercut the premium clip buds on the market, but will set you back more than the true bargain buds. It’s a competitive price point and the competition section later will run you through some alternatives.
You’ll see that there’s no US price there. Xiaomi doesn’t sell its tech in the US. The regional pricing converts to about $160 though, if you choose to import from elsewhere. How does that look in the market? The four-star Shokz OpenDots Air also sell for $129.95 / £129.99 / AU$219, while the Anker Soundcore Aeroclip 2 (also in receipt of a four-star review from the TechRadar team) are a little pricier, at $169.99 / £159.99 (about AU$240).
What I'm saying is, there's an open goal here for a decent product at the level — and Xiaomi's just scored the winner..
Xiaomi Clip review: Specs
| Drivers | 11mm | 
| Active noise cancellation | No | 
| Battery life | 9 hours (buds), 38 hours (case) | 
| Weight | 5.8g (buds) 64g (case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Frequency response | 20-48kHz | 
| Waterproofing | IP57 | 
Xiaomi Clip review: Features
- 6-hour battery life isn't amazing
- ANC is surprisingly solid
- App has EQ including useful presets
Xiaomi puts the Clip's battery life at 9 hours per bud, and I'd largely concur based on my own testing. The case itself brings that figure up to 38 hours, both of which are roughly average for this kind of earbud.
Usually in an earbuds review I'd talk about ANC next, but as is the case with most open-ears, there's no noise cancellation here. There's something similar, in a sound leakage tool, but we'll talk more about that later.
The Xiaomi Earbuds app brings you plenty of extra tools for the earbuds; sometimes these apps feel optional, but in the Clip's case, the app is really worth a download.
Many of the 'standard' app features are here: there's the ability to change what the touch controls do, change between audio presets, toggle settings like in-ear detection, and play an alarm if you've lost your earbuds.
Notably, the missing feature is an equalizer; if you want anything beyond 'Enhance Treble' or 'Enhance Voice', you're out of luck. People who like to tweak their sound won't be happy with this, and it's an odd omission for any kind of earbuds.
So what makes the app worth downloading, then? Well, it's to use the audio recording tool. This lets you use the earbuds or case to record what's going on around you, as well as from calls or videos you're watching. Obviously, you'll need to abide by local laws when you're doing that kind of thing in calls, but I found it very useful for leaving myself voice memos on the fly.
- Features score: 4 / 5
Xiaomi Clip review: Design
- Tiny, light carry case
- Reliable fit, though sometimes slight pinch
- Each bud is one-directional
The Xiaomi Clip comes in the smallest carry case I’ve seen for clipping earbuds. It’s a small square box of textured plastic, which opens in a clamshell style and weighs 52g. It bears a USB-C port for charging, as well as a grille for the microphone (more on that later).
Given its size and shape, it bears more than a passing resemblance to an engagement ring box — don’t hand it to a loved one for fear of sending the wrong message — but I appreciate how small and portable it is.
You can pick the earbuds up in four colors: Sand Gold, which you see in pictures, as well as Pearl White, Graphite Black and Frost Purple. The gold model is shiny and reflective: impossible to photograph for review images without being in the snaps yourself. It's a little bit like jewelry (think stylish ear cuff, perhaps?) but I must concede that there's a small chance you could consider it overly blingy, depending on your tastes.
Now, onto the earbuds: given that these are clip-style earbuds, you can probably (and correctly) predict that they’re C-shaped units which clip to your ear. There’s a counterweight, and the driver unit which goes into your ear-well (or the lower part of your concha, the cavum).
Some open earbuds have softer, flexible arches, but that’s not the case here, and thus the buds aren’t as malleable as many alternatives. I thought that’d make them a little uncomfortable to wear, and there was initially a little pinch when I put them on, but my fears were thankfully unfounded. They sit firmly in the ear too, and I never had any stability issues.
The buds have some on-ear controls too: you can double or triple tap each earbud for different functions. My taps were generally picked up, even when I had gloves on, but sometimes they didn't work perfectly.
If there’s one small frustration, it’s that there’s a right bud and a left bud; most clip-style open ears can be used in either ear. It means you constantly have to check which bud is which, and make sure you’re putting the correct one in the right ear. It’s not a huge chore, but it’s something you don’t need to do in most rivals.
- Design score: 5 / 5
Xiaomi Clip review: Sound quality
- 11mm driver per bud
- V-shaped sound profile
- No support for LDAC playback
Xiaomi has clearly changed tack from the OpenWear Stereo Pro’s ‘the more drivers, the merrier’ approach. Each Clip bud has a single 11mm driver, instead of multiple drivers to hit each point of the sonic spectrum.
It doesn’t matter, though, because the Xiaomi Clip are some of the best sounding open earbuds I’ve tested to date. They give you exactly what you expect from earbuds designed for active wear: a rich V-shaped sound.
Bass is clearly emphasised in a way that’d be a little too much in normal earbuds, but works well to compensate for how much low-end gets lost due to the form factor. In a song like ALO’s Girl, I Wanna Lay You Down, the rhythmic bass stands out even if you’re listening while cycling down a busy high street. One of my favorite running songs, Lack of Water by The Why Store, had more of a punch than many other open-ears offer.
Then there’s the other side of the valley, treble: it’s crisp and clear enough to hold its own against the low-end, with plenty of detail to catch vocal flair and string timbre. I’ve been enjoying listening to the soundtrack to Tenzing and the Xiaomi Clip are some of the only open earbuds which could do justice to the music.
Of course, there’s also the bottom of the V-shaped valley, and it’s the mids. These aren’t as prominent in the mix, with songs often losing their accompanying rhythmic instruments. Hey, I’d be more critical of this in standard earbuds, where you want to hear the totality of a song — in open-ears, which are more often for people working out or in busy areas, I can be more forgiving.
The Xiaomi Clip don’t let you play via LDAC; instead, they’re stuck to AAC, SBC or LHDC. The latter's quite rare in earbuds; it's similar to LDAC but works offers lower latencies and doesn't have as high a bitrate. It's close, but not quite LDAC.
Like the OpenWear Stereo Pro, they have a neat noise leak reduction feature, which stops people around you from hearing your music as loud, solving a common open earbuds problem.
- Sound quality: 4.5 / 5
Xiaomi Clip review: Value
- Priced as mid-range clip earbuds
- Some cheaper options offer better value...
- ... but it's still good here
I'm not going to pretend that the Xiaomi Clip are the best-value open earbuds on the market. I've reviewed models that cost a fair bit less, which were also worth buying.
However they're still great value when you bear in mind that they're basically premium open-ears, at a middle-of-the-road cost. They're a worthy alternative to the Ultras of the market, but without the high price.
- Value: 4 / 5
Should I buy the Xiaomi Clip?
| Xiaomi Clip score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Features | The battery life is average and the app has some useful tools, including a recorder, but the lack of an equalizer hurts. | 4/5 | 
| Design | The earbuds come in a tiny carry case, fit really well, and have a reliable touch button. I've not tested a better-designed pair (as long as you don't mind shiny buds). | 5/5 | 
| Sound quality | The sound will please fitness users, with hefty bass and crisp treble. | 4.5/5 | 
| Value | The Xiaomi Clip are no budget buds, but they give you what you want for a price that's not prohibitive. | 4/5 | 
Buy them if…
You want bassy open earbuds
Bass is often lacking in open-ears, but I found it sufficient in the Xiaomi Clip.
You need a small carry case
Pocketable and light, the carry case is one of the smallest I've seen in open-ears, plus it's nice-looking.
You like earbuds with audio recording
Audio-recording earbuds are becoming more common, and the Xiaomi are some of the first cuff-style buds to offer it.
Don’t buy them if…
You need an equalizer
It's an odd feature to be missing. Plenty of people use equalizers to change how their earbuds sounds, but you can't here.
You don't like their blingy nature
While wearing the earbuds, I had a few comments about how blingy they looked. If you're not a fan of their shiny jewelry sheen, there are alternatives.
Xiaomi Clip review: Also consider
Looking for alternative clip-style buds? Here are a few alternatives at the same price point.
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Xiaomi Clip | Shokz OpenDots Air | Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Drivers | 11mm | 2x 11.8mm | 12mm | 
| Active noise cancellation | No | No | No | 
| Battery life (ANC on) | 9 hours (buds) / 38 hours (case) | 9 hours (buds) / 36 hours (case) | 8 hours (buds) / 32 hours (case) | 
| Weight | 5.8g (buds) 64g (case) | 6.3g (buds) 37.3g (case) | 6.2g (bud) 37.9g (case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 5.4 | Bluetooth 6.1 | Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Waterproofing | IP57 | IP55 | IP57 | 
Shokz OpenDots Air
Another option which sells for the same price as the Xiaomi, the OpenDots Air are an even more comfortable fit than the Xiaomi, though I wasn't bowled over by the audio quality.
Read our full Shokz OpenDots Air review
Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2
A slightly more premium option, the AeroClip 2 have a comfortable, secure fit and also offer an equalizer. In fact, they have a listening test. 
Read our full Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 review
How I tested the Xiaomi Clip
- Tested for three weeks
- Paired with Samsung phone
- Used on runs, cycles and at home
I used the Xiaomi Clip for three weeks before writing this review, and they were connected to my Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra throughout the testing process.
To test the Clip I did some listening at home, but most of the use was on runs or while cycling. I'd estimate I used them for about an hour a day during the three weeks. I mostly listened to music via Spotify or my library of lossless music, but also played some games and watched videos too.
I've been reviewing audio gadgets for years, including open earbuds from the first few models, and I've also been testing Xiaomi phones and earbuds for years too. Several of the Xiaomi Clip's contemporaries were also reviewed by me.
- First reviewed in November 2026
Tom Bedford is a freelance contributor covering tech, entertainment and gaming. Beyond TechRadar, he has bylines on sites including GamesRadar, Digital Trends, Android Police, TechAdvisor, WhattoWatch and BGR. From 2019 to 2022 he was on the TechRadar team as the staff writer and then deputy editor for the mobile team.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, le sèche-cheveux Dyson Supersonic Nural tombe à 284 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le sèche cheveux Dyson Supersonic Nural à 284,00 € (-14%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le sèche-cheveux Dyson Supersonic Nural passe à 284,00 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 14 % et 46,33 € d'économie. Efficace pour sécher rapidement avec une température stable qui protège le cuir chevelu, il affiche une note actuelle de 4,5/5 dans nos tests.
Dyson fait évoluer son célèbre appareil de coiffure avec le Supersonic Nural. Ce sèche-cheveux intègre de nouveaux capteurs pour réguler automatiquement la chaleur du flux d'air et préserver le cuir chevelu. Ce modèle avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage en test.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Dyson Supersonic Nural descend à 284,00 € chez Amazon, soit environ 14 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (330,33 €). Cela représente une économie de 46,33 €.
Séchage maîtrisé et température stable au banc d'essai
Le Dyson Supersonic Nural s'appuie sur une puissance de 1600 W pour délivrer un souffle d'air homogène qui réduit le temps passé sous l'appareil. Le système de capteurs ajuste en direct la chaleur pour éviter les montées excessives qui abîment la fibre capillaire. Comme souligné dans notre test complet, la température reste parfaitement stable au cours de la session.
L'ergonomie générale profite d'une bonne maniabilité au quotidien. L'appareil est livré avec un concentrateur, un diffuseur, un peigne à dents larges, un embout cheveux sensibles et un embout lissant qui se fixent rapidement grâce à un système aimanté.
Dyson Supersonic Nural
Points forts
- Design et maniabilité.
- Embouts aimantés.
- Accessoires nombreux.
- Séchage puissant et homogène.
- Température stable.
Points faibles
- Bruit entêtant à la longue.
- Les commandes sont noyées sur la façade transparente.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une interface plus dense et un niveau sonore présent
Ce modèle propose trois niveaux de vitesse et trois réglages de température manuels pour s'adapter à la texture de chaque chevelure. La façade transparente accueille désormais les boutons de commande, ce qui rend leur lecture immédiate un peu moins évidente lors des premières utilisations.
Le bruit émis par le moteur peut aussi devenir entêtant lors de longues sessions de coiffage. Ce sèche-cheveux convient parfaitement à ceux qui cherchent un séchage rapide et respectueux du cuir chevelu, mais demandera un temps d'adaptation à ceux qui privilégient un fonctionnement silencieux.
Dyson Supersonic : l'autre option face au Dyson Supersonic Nural
Le premier Dyson Supersonic reste une référence solide pour qui veut un flux d'air puissant et une température maîtrisée sans recourir à des capteurs d'ajustement automatique. Il est vendu 266,99 €, soit 17,01 € de moins que le Supersonic Nural à son prix du jour.
Le Supersonic Nural apporte l'automatisation de la chauffe pour protéger le cuir chevelu sans réglage manuel, mais le Dyson Supersonic conserve la même note actuelle de 4,5/5 pour un tarif inférieur de 17,01 €.
Dyson Supersonic
Points forts
- Design et maniabilité.
- Embouts aimantés.
- Accessoires nombreux.
- Séchage puissant et homogène.
- Température stable.
Points faibles
- Bruit pas toujours agréable à la longue.

articles.title: Mientras GTA 6 es un éxito en ventas, 1.600 empleados de Rockstar temen quedar sin trabajo
articles.text:
Rockstar Games vive un contraste que resume el momento actual de la industria de los videojuegos: mientras Grand Theft Auto VI rompe todos los récords de ventas, más de 1.600 trabajadores de la compañía en Reino Unido votan si formar un sindicato porque temen perder su empleo.
La votación comenzó el 12 de noviembre y cierra el 26, apenas días después del estreno del juego el 19 de noviembre en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Si el resultado es favorable, según el sindicato impulsor, sería el mayor gremio reconocido del sector de los videojuegos británico.
Un lanzamiento que pulverizó cifras históricas
Take-Two Interactive, empresa matriz de Rockstar, confirmó que las ventas minoristas del primer día de GTA VI alcanzaron los 3.790 millones de dólares, con 32,5 millones de copias vendidas antes de su salida, un récord para cualquier plataforma. La cifra superó incluso las estimaciones más optimistas de firmas como Sensor Tower, que había calculado unos 1.840 millones de dólares y 19 millones de copias para el estreno.
Para dimensionar el salto: GTA V, lanzado en 2013, había tardado tres días en superar los 1.000 millones de dólares. Su sucesor multiplicó esa marca casi por cinco en apenas 24 horas, aunque buena parte de esas ventas corresponde a preventas acumuladas desde junio.
Por qué los trabajadores piden sindicalizarse
El pedido de reconocimiento voluntario del Rockstar Game Workers Union, parte del Sindicato Independiente de Trabajadores de Gran Bretaña (IWGB), se presentó en junio. Los reclamos incluyen mayor transparencia salarial, un trato más justo frente al crunch (las jornadas extenuantes previas a un lanzamiento) y condiciones de trabajo más flexibles.
Nestor Uriarte, programador de animación en el estudio de Edimburgo, explicó en una columna de opinión que incluso quienes trabajan en “el juego más grande de todos los tiempos” temen ser despedidos. Uriarte recordó que GTA V vendió más de 230 millones de copias y generó más de 10.000 millones de dólares en todo el mundo, una cifra que, según su argumento, debería traducirse en mejores condiciones para quienes lo hicieron posible.
El temor tiene respaldo estadístico. La encuesta State of the Game Industry 2026, realizada por la Game Developers Conference a más de 2.300 profesionales, reveló que el 28% había sido despedido en los dos años anteriores y que el 52% considera que la inteligencia artificial generativa está perjudicando a la industria.
Uriarte sostuvo que un sindicato con reconocimiento permitiría a los trabajadores tener voz en la transición hacia la automatización, en momentos en que estudios de todo el sector eliminaron un estimado de 24.000 puestos de trabajo en dos años.
El tribunal que investiga los despidos de 2025
La votación sindical coincide con la etapa final de un juicio laboral en Glasgow. En octubre de 2025, Rockstar despidió a un grupo de empleados en Reino Unido y Canadá, cifra que la empresa y el sindicato ubican en distintos números: el IWGB habla de 31 despedidos, mientras que la defensa de la compañía mencionó 34 personas afectadas en Rockstar North.
El IWGB, que representa a 23 de esos trabajadores en el proceso, sostiene que los despidos respondieron a su organización sindical en un canal privado de Discord. Rockstar, en cambio, asegura que la medida se debió a la filtración de información confidencial en ese mismo espacio.
Los alegatos finales se escucharon el 17 y 18 de noviembre, en la misma semana del estreno del juego. El abogado de Rockstar, Thomas Cordrey, afirmó que los empleados fueron “atrapados con las manos en la masa” al incumplir políticas de confidencialidad en un servidor con cientos de miembros, donde se discutieron funciones no publicadas de GTA VI y la fecha de su lanzamiento.
Cordrey agregó que la compañía atravesaba “una presión enorme” y estaba “al borde de anunciar más retrasos” cuando se detectaron esas filtraciones, y que la alternativa habría sido afrontar 34 audiencias disciplinarias extensas con un desenlace inevitable. También citó el testimonio de Jennifer Kolbe, jefa de licencias de Rockstar, quien declaró haberse sentido “conmocionada y consternada” al descubrir el contenido del servidor.
Rockstar emitió un comunicado en el que sostuvo que los despidos respondieron a “falta grave” por compartir información confidencial de la compañía, no a la actividad sindical de los afectados. La empresa remarcó que su posición “ha sido clara y constante” durante todo el proceso y que se mantiene “confiada en un resultado positivo”.
Las evidencias concluyeron el 18 de noviembre y no se fijó un plazo para el fallo, que podría demorar varias semanas. El resultado de la votación sindical se conocerá el 26 de noviembre, apenas una semana después de que GTA VI estableciera el mayor debut de la historia del entretenimiento.

articles.title: 17-year-old Windows 7 gets unofficial DirectX 12 and Vulkan 1.4 support — enthusiasts bring Nvidia RTX 50, AMD RX 9000, and Intel Arc GPUs to the aging OS
articles.text:
17-year-old Windows 7 gets unofficial DirectX 12 and Vulkan 1.4 support — enthusiasts bring Nvidia RTX 50, AMD RX 9000, and Intel Arc GPUs to the aging OS
Windows 7 gets a second wind with modern GPU support.
Windows 7 may have been retired years ago, but that hasn’t stopped enthusiasts from finding ways to bring modern hardware and features to Microsoft’s beloved operating system. A new community project is now giving Windows 7 the ability to support modern Nvidia, AMD, and Intel graphics cards, along with DirectX 12 and Vulkan 1.4 capabilities.
Developed by enthusiasts EAZY BLACK, kryptik, and VisualEhrmanntraut, the project backports WDDM 2.2 from Windows 10. Interestingly, Windows 7 originally launched with WDDM 1.1, while Microsoft introduced WDDM 2.0 with Windows 10 in 2015 and WDDM 2.2 with the Creators Update in 2017. Microsoft also introduced a limited version of DirectX 12 for Windows 7 in 2019; however, that implementation was only meant for developers to port select games to the older operating system.
According to a post by @TheBobPony on X, Nvidia's RTX 40 and RTX 50 series, AMD's Radeon RX 7000 and RX 9000 series, and select Intel Arc graphics cards are supported. Screenshots confirm that the backport enables GPUs to be recognized by Windows 7 as well as third-party apps like GPU-Z. It is also claimed that features such as ray tracing and DLSS also work on compatible hardware. Older GPUs, including Nvidia's RTX 30 series and AMD's Radeon RX 6000 series, may also benefit from the project. That said, actual feature support depends on the graphics card, driver implementation, and application.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
For anyone who still prefers Windows 7 or relies on older software and hardware, this project is worth exploring, especially if you intend to extend the usefulness of the operating system. Users can also combine it with the VxKex compatibility layer, allowing newer Windows apps to run on older operating systems. You can grab the project files and modified drivers by heading to the W7Revived website.
There’s a reason why enthusiasts continue to keep Windows 7 alive. Released in 2009 as a successor to Windows Vista, it offered a familiar interface, solid performance, and a straightforward desktop experience. It became one of Microsoft’s most popular operating systems and remained a favorite among PC enthusiasts and everyday users long after the arrival of Windows 10.
In fact, Windows 7 still has some life left in it. We recently tested the aging operating system against Windows 11 on a modern PC running on an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Radeon RX 6950 XT, and 64GB of DDR5 memory. The tests included eight DirectX 11 and two DirectX 9 titles, with Windows 7 delivering better performance in certain scenarios, particularly CPU-bound games, along with stronger 1% lows in some titles.

Kunal Khullar is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. He is a long time technology journalist and reviewer specializing in PC components and peripherals, and welcomes any and every question around building a PC.

articles.title: Ce robot-tondeuse s'en sort bien… quand il a du réseau
articles.text:
| Surface de tonte maximale | 1500 m2 | 
| Gestion des zones | 80 | 
| Système de tonte | lames pivotantes | 
| Connectivité | Bluetooth, GSM, Wi-Fi | 
| Pente maximale | 65 % | 
| Hauteur de coupe minimale/maximale | 30 / 90 mm | 
| Dimensions (L x l x H) | 718 x 470 x 352 mm | 
| Masse | 18.5 kg | 
| Batterie | 10 Ah | 
| Autonomie | 2 heures | 
| Durée de la charge | 120 min | 
| Largeur de coupe | 22 cm | 
| Réglage de hauteur de coupe | électrique | 
| Largeur minimale de passage étroit | 150 cm | 
| Gestion des zones annexes | Oui | 
| Niveau sonore | 65 | 
| Antivol | Verrouillage position GPS, Verrouillage smartphone | 
| GPS | Oui | 
| Abri | en option | 
| Tonte sous la pluie | Non | 
| Nettoyage au jet d'eau | Oui | 
| Indice de réparabilité | 8 /10 | 
Avec ses roues à galets et son large pare-chocs, le robot-tondeuse Airseekers Tron SE a des airs de buggy. Nous lui avons confié notre pelouse avec de l'herbe haute à tondre et un sol que la pluie n'a guère épargné.
Paré d’une coque argentée sur un châssis ajouré, de bandes lumineuses de part et d'autre des caméras et d’un pare-chocs qui déborde du capot, le Tron SE a de l'allure. Certains préféreront plus de discrétion au jardin, question de goût. L'originalité se trouve aussi sous la machine, où Airseekers a glissé une pale derrière le disque de coupe pour brasser l'herbe fraîchement tondue.
Affiché à 1399 €, le Tron SE vise, selon Airseekers, les jardins d'environ 1500 m². La marque annonce jusqu'à 400 m² par charge avec la batterie de 10 Ah. Sur une parcelle qui approche la surface recommandée, il faudra donc compter plusieurs sorties. La hauteur de coupe, elle, se règle de 3 à 9 cm, de quoi garder un peu de longueur en été ou reprendre progressivement une pelouse qui a bien poussé.
Pour se repérer, le robot associe ses caméras à un positionnement par satellites corrigé en temps réel, notre modèle ayant reçu ces corrections par Internet via le service NetRTK. Il n'y a alors ni câble à enterrer le long de la pelouse ni antenne à dresser. Le manuel prévoit aussi une version RTK classique avec son mât et son récepteur. Nous n'avons toutefois trouvé sur la boutique de la marque ni cette déclinaison du SE ni le module seul.
Le Tron SE mesure près de 72 cm de long et 47 cm de large pour 18,5 kg annoncés. Les deux roues motrices de 22,5 cm sont à l'arrière, reconnaissables à leurs profondes sculptures. À l'avant, de petits galets disposés tout autour des roues leur permettent de glisser latéralement dans les virages. Malgré ses airs de 4 x 4, le Tron SE utilise donc bien une simple propulsion.
La poignée arrière s'avère très pratique lorsqu'il faut déplacer l'engin. La batterie, quant à elle, se retire en libérant un loquet dans son compartiment. On peut ainsi rentrer uniquement l'accumulateur ou le remplacer sans avoir à démonter la carrosserie (comptez 299 € sur la boutique officielle). La boîte du Tron SE comprend également les fixations de la station, les outils d'assemblage, ainsi que des lames et des vis de rechange.
La station se résume à une plaque à fixer au sol et une petite colonne sur laquelle viennent s'appuyer les contacts de charge, situés à l'arrière du robot. L'ensemble a trouvé discrètement sa place au pied de notre terrasse ; il lui faut simplement une surface plane et de l'espace devant la plaque pour faciliter les manœuvres.
Les connecteurs de l'alimentation et de l'éventuel module RTK sont accessibles derrière un cache. Le câble fourni est court et, surtout, le bloc d'alimentation tombe à quelques centimètres de la station. Pas facile dans ces conditions de le mettre à l'abri des intempéries. La rallonge, qui permet d'éloigner le bloc, est vendue en supplément à 49 €.
L'appairage est assez simple à portée du wifi. L'application demande d'activer le Bluetooth et d'autoriser la localisation, puis de scanner le QR code logé dans le compartiment de la batterie. Celui que l'on voit sur la coque, près du bouton Stop, renvoie à l'assistance. On peut aussi saisir le numéro de série manuellement. Les identifiants wifi sont ensuite transmis au robot via le Bluetooth.
Avant de laisser sortir le Tron SE, l'application vérifie sa présence sur la base, la liaison Bluetooth, le positionnement RTK et le niveau de batterie, qui doit atteindre au moins 20 %. On bascule ensuite le téléphone à l'horizontale. Deux joysticks permettent de longer les limites de la pelouse et, à moins de 1 m du point de départ, le logiciel propose de fermer le contour.
Pendant notre première cartographie, l'application a quitté l'interface de pilotage avant de se relancer. Le même incident s'est produit lors de l'ajout d'une zone.
Une perte de réseau pourrait l’expliquer, car le smartphone pilote le robot en Bluetooth, mais les corrections NetRTK arrivent par le wifi de la maison ou par la propre connexion 4G du Tron SE. Or cette dernière était désactivée sur notre exemplaire. À la limite de portée de la box, le robot pouvait donc perdre l'accès aux corrections, alors même que nous marchions juste à côté.
Si le wifi ne couvre pas tout le jardin, reste la possibilité d'utiliser la 4G. Ce forfait est toutefois payant dès le premier mois. L'app affiche 4,40 $ pour un mois et 100 Mo, ou 55 $ pour un an et 1800 Mo. Ceux dont le wifi porte jusqu'au bout de la pelouse pourront, fort heureusement, se passer de cet abonnement pour utiliser le NetRTK.
À côté du gros bouton Stop, trois touches permettent d'allumer ou valider, de lancer la tonte et rappeler le robot sans smartphone. Pour démarrer, il faut presser la touche de travail, puis OK dans la seconde qui suit.
Les bandes lumineuses ont leur utilité. Le bleu accompagne l'appairage, le jaune indique une pause et le rouge signale une erreur ou une action à réaliser. À la station, le vert clignote pendant la charge et devient fixe une fois la batterie pleine. On retrouve l'éclairage dans les réglages de l'application, ainsi qu'un mode nuit autorisant la tonte après la tombée du jour.
Heureusement, toute modification ne demande pas de relancer le robot. Une fois la carte enregistrée, on peut placer une zone interdite, scinder une parcelle ou en fusionner deux du bout du doigt.
Pour étendre la carte à une nouvelle portion de pelouse, il faut en revanche en tracer le contour au joystick. Le menu permet aussi de nommer chaque zone et d'ajouter un “canal”, le terme choisi au lieu de “chemin” pour désigner le passage reliant deux surfaces.
La hauteur se règle pour toute la pelouse ou zone par zone. Un menu baptisé Efficacité de la tonte propose trois profils selon que le gazon est standard, dense ou clairsemé. L'intervalle entre les passages, l'évitement d'obstacles, les virages ou encore l'ordre de coupe ont aussi leur entrée. Il manque toutefois parfois une phrase explicative pour comprendre ce que changera concrètement un réglage.
Le sens de tonte est mieux illustré. Il suffit de tourner un cadran gradué pour voir les bandes pivoter sur la carte et les aligner avec le grand côté de la pelouse. Sur un terrain en L comme le nôtre, l'angle qui convient à une branche peut multiplier les demi-tours dans l'autre. La tonte adaptative permet alors au robot de diviser la surface en sections et de choisir une orientation optimale pour chacune.
Las, la traduction réserve quelques surprises. Pour retrouver l'historique des tontes, qui aurait l'idée de chercher du côté de “durée de vie du robot” ? Le centre d'entretien se montre heureusement plus explicite. Il décompte les heures avant de s'occuper des roues, des caméras ou du plateau. Quant à la localisation GPS annoncée en cas de vol, nous n'avons pas pu y accéder dans les paramètres. L'absence de forfait 4G actif pourrait logiquement l'expliquer, mais l'app ne nous a guère éclairés sur ce point.
En relevant l'avant du robot, on découvre un disque central à trois lames pivotantes. Rapporté aux 47 cm de large de la machine, ce dernier paraît bien modeste avec ses 22 cm de diamètre. Les lames restent en retrait des flancs et le disque ne se déporte pas. Au pied d'un mur ou au bord d'une terrasse qui empêche les roues de déborder, une bande de pelouse échappe donc logiquement à la coupe. Un plateau plus large est toutefois vendu séparément à 49 €.
Une pale met l'air en mouvement dans le carter pour que les brins coupés y circulent, soient recoupés, puis retombent sur la pelouse. C'est le principe du mulching, baptisé FlowCut par Airseekers. Si l'idée de mieux répartir les résidus s'avère intéressante sur le papier, il est difficile d'en apprécier le véritable bénéfice sur un gazon où il n'y a que quelques millimètres à enlever au quotidien.
Notre balle de tennis a eu droit aux égards que l'on attend d'une tondeuse équipée de caméras. Le Tron SE l'a bien reconnue et contournée. Même constat au pied de l'arbuste, où la machine a su éviter le petit tronc qui se trouvait sur son passage.
L'herbe haute n'arrête pas systématiquement le Tron SE pour autant. Le manuel donne un repère à hauteur de roue, soit à environ 15 cm du sol. À cette hauteur, une herbe peu dense peut encore être abordée sereinement avec le réglage de coupe le plus haut.
Notre massif de fougères a visiblement eu droit au même traitement que le gazon. Le robot s'y est engagé, les branches sont passées de part et d'autre du pare-chocs, puis l'engin s'est coincé sans parvenir à les couper. Voilà une plantation qui mérite sa zone interdite.
Notre période d'essai a été particulièrement pluvieuse. Sur les parties meubles ou gorgées d'eau, le Tron SE a malheureusement marqué le jardin à plusieurs reprises. La terre humide se loge entre les crampons des roues arrière jusqu'à les combler. Les roues perdent alors leur accroche, patinent et creusent le sol à l'endroit même où le robot cherche à repartir.
Le capteur de pluie peut commander le retour à la station pendant une averse. Le lendemain, même sous un ciel dégagé, mieux vaut vérifier que le terrain a bien séché avant de relancer une tonte.
L'Airseekers Tron SE conviendra avant tout à un jardin au sol ferme et où le wifi porte jusqu'au bout de la pelouse. Sur notre terrain détrempé, ses roues arrière se sont effectivement chargées de terre, au point de patiner et creuser des sillons. Côté réseau, la 4G permet d'étendre la portée du NetRTK au-delà de celle de la box, moyennant un abonnement payant dès le premier mois. La carte, une fois enregistrée, se retouche facilement du bout du doigt. Sur la pelouse, le Tron SE a su contourner notre balle de tennis comme le petit tronc de l'arbuste. Le premier passage requiert toutefois un peu de vigilance pour identifier les zones interdites.
Destiné aux jardins jusqu'à 1600 m², l'Ecovacs Goat A1600 Lidar Pro se guide grâce à son LiDAR et sa caméra sans dépendre du signal satellitaire. Il possède également un système de tonte des bordures avancé. Toujours autour de ce tarif, le modèle Eufy E18 navigue lui aussi sans RTK et peut assurer la tonte de jardins de 1200 m².

articles.title: Europe's biggest AI challenge isn't the technology. It's organizational psychology
articles.text:
Europe's biggest AI challenge isn't the technology. It's organizational psychology
Why Europe’s AI ambitions depend on understanding employees
Despite years of discussions and pilot projects, only 25% of EU workers use artificial intelligence (AI) for work purposes, compared to 43% of employees in the US. The gap is not simply about access to better tools or frontier models but reflects how organizations manage change.
President EMEA at Cognizant.
Too many European organizations make the same fundamental mistake, conflating access to AI with its adoption. Often, this comes across as broad mandates to employees, asking them to be more productive through AI but then leaving them to figure out what that means for their role. Our own research has found that over a third of employees are still looking for clear reasons to adopt AI.
If Europe wants to persuade its workforce that AI is an enabler rather than a threat, then it needs to rethink how it builds confidence, trust and motivation across the workforce.
Understand workers’ concerns
Every employee approaches work, risk and technology in unique ways. Their fears and concerns vary depending on stage of career, level of tech skill and more.
Despite these differences, 41% of workers in the EU are at least somewhat concerned about job displacement due to AI, with some of the highest fear appearing among younger individuals preparing to enter the job market.
Meanwhile, current workers are split on attitudes towards the technology. Our research found over 60 different personas, grouped into seven broad archetypes. Some readily adopt AI tools, while others are more cautious or need more persuading. There are also workers who are simply unsure where to begin their journey or how it fits into their working life.
Age and career stage also shape these attitudes. As Europe’s workforce grows older, some experienced employees may worry about becoming obsolete or question the value of learning entirely new ways of working late in their careers. This makes it harder to change long-established working habits.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Finally, even when workers do want to use AI, 82% report they are regularly unsatisfied with the tools they are actually given. This can quickly lead to them being put off further adoption due to these bad experiences and slow future roll-outs further.
Without intentional support, no matter how many tools businesses buy, they will still fail to see a return on investment.
Get the workforce onside
Leaders need to understand workers’ anxiety is not unfounded. Cognizant predicted in 2023 that by 2032, 90% of jobs would be disrupted by AI. But more recent research found that that target was reached six years ahead of schedule.
Leaders can’t gloss over that, and if they want to bridge the gap between employees and AI initiatives, they need to start building trust, which starts with honesty. Executives should be clear about what has been decided, what remains uncertain and where automation is still being tested. This gives employees the information needed to understand where they fit, how their role could change and what support will be available.
This must also be supported by reskilling, support and development pathways to ensure enterprises are preparing their workforces for these new ways of working. This doesn’t mean a complete change to a person’s career but instead ensuring they have the skills necessary to combine AI capabilities with their existing domain expertise.
The conversation around AI also needs to be reframed. Rather than focusing on automation, leaders should prioritize improving effectiveness, expanding capabilities and elevating the quality and impact of human work.
Build for behavior, not technology
Businesses need to change how they approach transformation. Principally, this means moving from individual tech projects to business wide change across all teams. The first step of this process is leadership teams adapting their mindset from AI being the solution to their problems to building for outcomes which are enabled by AI.
This can be done in three simple steps:
Define an intention architecture. Instead of focusing the program on what the technology can do, successful organizations anchor it in what they want people to do differently. They design from desired behavioral outcomes backward, clarifying the human actions, decisions and workflows AI should change.
Normalize experimentation. Most teams don’t feel psychologically safe enough to try, fail and iterate in the open. High‑performing organizations create structured spaces where experimentation is expected, supported and de‑risked. This makes learning part of the job, not a side project.
Model the behavior through managers and influencers. People adopt what they see, not what they’re told. When managers and respected peers actively use AI tools in their day‑to‑day work, the shift becomes cultural rather than policy‑driven.
Shifting the mindset for the future
Europe will not close its AI adoption gap simply by giving more employees access to more powerful tools. It will close it when organizations give people a clear reason to use AI, the confidence to experiment and an honest account of how work will change. The technology is ready. The determining factor will be whether leaders can bring their workforce with them.

articles.title: Hace 2.000 años en Menorca despedían a los suyos por todo lo alto: funerales con vino y leche
articles.text:
En Alaior, un pequeño pueblo situado en la costa sur de Menorca, además de unas playas espectaculares hay una necrópolis de cuevas artificiales excavadas en la roca en Cales Coves. Pues bien, ese yacimiento acaba de dejarnos un descubrimiento de lo más llamativo sobre cómo eran los funerales hace 2.000 años. En una frase: se lo montaban a lo grande.
El hallazgo. Delante de la cueva 45 hay un patio abierto que, como cuenta la arqueóloga Sònia Carbonell al diari Ara, se creó expresamente para realizar rituales de despedida. Quienes acudieron a esos funerales dejaron unas vasijas cuyo contenido no se había identificado hasta ahora.
Un equipo de la UAB, el Barcelona Supercomputing Center y la Universitat Pompeu Fabra ha analizado los residuos orgánicos de 34 vasijas de cerámica de esa cueva y ha descubierto que los pequeños contenían principalmente lácteos, además de trazas de vino en otras vasijas que tenían formas inspiradas en el Mediterráneo, sobre todo en el mundo púnico. Una de las piezas con pico vertedor, de la que se pensaba inicialmente que era una aceitera, tenía una mezcla de lácteos con fruta y se cree que probablemente hiciera las veces de biberón.
Por qué importa. Porque es la primera vez en la isla que se documenta el uso del vino en un ritual funerario menorquín. Hay que tener en cuenta que por aquel entonces el vino era un producto de fuera, de uso más ocasional. La leche, por el contrario, era un producto básico y cotidiano (concretamente, la de cabra y oveja).
Los menorquines de la época copiaron recipientes extranjeros, pero los usaron a su manera. Como sintetiza Carbonell, la comunidad integraba productos y formas de fuera manteniendo sus códigos culturales y su identidad. Que hubiera un biberón sugiere que en ese momento de la despedida también se quería recordar el cuidado de los niños.
Cómo lo descubrieron. Estas piezas se recuperaron entre 2023 y 2024 y muchas de ellas no solo estaban intactas, sino que seguían en su posición original. Después, escanearon los objetos, los microexcavaron y los analizaron químicamente. Además de lácteos y vino, identificaron grasas animales y aceites vegetales varios.
Los completos y complejos funerales menorquines. Dentro de la lista de Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO están los restos de la cultura talayótica de Menorca, que tenía unos rituales funerarios bastante complejos, como teñir de rojo el pelo de quienes fallecían o cortarles un mechón. Después, en el periodo posttalayótico, los contactos con el exterior aumentaron. Sin ir más lejos, Carbonell señalaba en una investigación anterior que la arquitectura funeraria sugería que hubo interacción con grupos púnicos.
Vaya por delante algo: este tipo de recipientes ya eran conocidos. De hecho, el Museu de Menorca estudió 269 vasos altos pertenecientes al al hipogeo de Sa Mola y los relacionó con una práctica funeraria de ofrendas y de banquetes La primera campaña de excavación en Cales Coves ya indicaba prácticas rituales entre los siglos IV-III y I a. C. Ahora sabemos que el patio y el interior de la cueva tenían funciones distintas: el biberón acompañaba al difunto dentro de la cámara a modo de ofrenda, mientras que en el patio tenía lugar el banquete, como evidencian los restos de cabras, ovejas y cerdos.
