articles.title: Your questions about Apple HomeView’s audio, answered
articles.text:
After I published my review of the HomeView, Apple’s first smart display, y’all still had a ton of questions about how it works as a smart speaker. So, I spent a bunch more time testing its audio capabilities and support for third-party music apps — and found a few more frustrations along the way. Here are the answers to all your burning questions. Have more? I’ll answer them in the comments.
Your questions about Apple HomeView’s audio, answered
The smart display sounds good and works well as a touchscreen music controller, but CarPlay apps are messy.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
How does the HomeView sound compared to the HomePod Mini, Sonos One, and HomePod?
The HomeView isn’t a replacement for a Sonos One, a full-size HomePod, or a similar-size speaker. Those are much better speakers. In size and sound, the HomeView is closer to the HomePod Mini. I tested it alongside the Mini 2 (which sounds marginally better than the first-gen Mini) and found the tabletop HomeView mostly comparable, with these caveats: The HomeView has better bass and is slightly louder, but it’s not as clear and is less room-filling.
You can hear them both in action in this video, alongside the full-size HomePod, the Sonos One, and the wall-mounted HomeView:
The difference comes down to the hardware. The Mini 2 has a single full-range driver and two passive radiators, whereas the tabletop HomeView has two drivers in the display, plus a woofer and two passive radiators in its base. While the woofer adds some oomph, the HomeView’s display, which sits over the speaker base, partly covers it, affecting the sound compared to the Mini. Apple added an accelerometer to the display because tilting it changes the sound, so HomeView adjusts its EQ in real time based on the angle. Still, the Mini, while not as loud, fills a room better, thanks partly to its 360-degree sound. (The HomeView supports Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos, which the Mini 2 doesn’t.)
The wall-mounted HomeView has only two drivers, with computational audio Apple says is “tuned specifically for on-wall placement.” It sounds fine but is noticeably thinner than the tabletop version, and bass is basically non-existent. I wouldn’t recommend it for its sound quality, but it’s great for talking to a visitor through your video doorbell.
Can you pair two HomeViews for stereo sound?
No. While you can group HomeViews with any other AirPlay speakers to play music out of them all at once, you can’t pair two for a stereo setup or pair a HomeView with a HomePod or Mini. I like the sound of two Minis paired in stereo and use this setup in my office and my bedroom. They also work as speakers for my Apple TVs in those rooms.
If you have $300 to spend on a good-sounding smart speaker setup, go with two Minis over a HomeView. The HomeView’s real benefit is the screen. I cover its uses extensively in my full review, but for audio in particular, I like that the screen acts like a jukebox, making it easy to change songs, select new music, and scroll through your podcasts or audiobooks — without needing to find a quarter! With a HomePod, you rely on Siri voice control or your Apple device to select content.
Can you AirPlay music/podcasts to the HomeView, and does audio handoff work?
You can AirPlay to the HomeView as with any other AirPlay speaker, and audio handoff works the same as it does on HomePods. Tap your phone to the HomeView, and whatever is playing transfers to the speakers and the screen. Handoff also works in reverse, letting you send any content back to your phone. One addition with the HomeView: You can now hand off video.
In testing, handoff worked for Apple TV, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pocket Casts, YouTube Music, FaceTime, and phone calls — although phone calls sometimes dropped. YouTube and YouTube TV videos also handed off, even though they don’t have an app on the HomeView. But Netflix and Amazon Prime Video only played audio, though both played video in the Safari browser.
One word of caution: Handoff is aggressive. As with HomePods, if you’re holding your phone within a few inches, the HomeView will try to hand off content.
Can you set a default speaker for the HomeView?
HomeView doesn’t let you set a default speaker or group to use instead of its built-in speaker. However, you can play audio to any AirPlay speaker or group of speakers. I tested this on HomePods, Sonos speakers, and a Samsung TV, and it worked smoothly.
For native apps (Apple Music, Podcasts, and Safari), the HomeView remembers the last speaker or speaker pair you used and automatically plays content through those when you return. If it’s been a while since you opened the app, it pops up the option to choose the last-used speakers.
Spotify has no search box because you’re not supposed to type while driving — only I’m not driving; I’m in my kitchen!
Things get messier with third-party audio apps such as Spotify and Audible, and with Apple apps that use the CarPlay interface, such as Apple News and Apple TV. The HomeView only automatically uses the last speakers if you choose content from the HomeView screen. If you use Siri voice control, it defaults to the HomeView speaker.
So, “Hey Siri, play ‘Femininomenon’ by Chappell Roan from Spotify” played music from HomeView’s speaker and not the stereo pair of Minis in my office, where I’d last been listening to Spotify. I could direct it to play music there by adding “on Office,” but that’s more of a mouthful than just “Hey Siri, play ‘Femininomenon’ by Chappell Roan,” which is all you need to say if you use Apple Music.
Which brings me to another one of your most-asked questions — and my biggest complaint about this device as a smart speaker: How does it support third-party audio apps? Like second-class citizens.
Does Spotify work on the HomeView?
Spotify works on the HomeView, but with limitations that apply to all non-native and third-party apps: they only show up when your phone is connected to the HomeView via your profile, so only you can use them.
Apple has taken a shortcut here: Rather than building a dedicated HomeView experience for app developers, the HomeView uses Apple’s existing CarPlay platform. This makes it easier for developers to put their apps on the HomeView — if an audio or video app supports CarPlay, it already works on the HomeView (there’s no support for other types of CarPlay apps).
In practice, this creates frustrating limitations, including no search function and the need for a user profile on the HomeView and your phone on the same Wi-Fi. It also results in slower performance and a laggy, inconsistent experience compared to the native apps.
I tried several apps: Pocket Casts, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, Spotify, and Audible. They all appeared in my HomeView app drawer, and I could access them, choose content via streamlined interfaces, and then play audio on the HomeView or AirPlay from it to any speakers.
But CarPlay apps don’t work as well as the built-in audio apps — Music, Podcasts, and Safari. They take longer to load and respond more slowly. You also can’t type a search query in any of them, as you can in the native apps, because they don’t have a search field or keyboard. Instead, you have to scroll through content to find what you want or use Siri voice search.
Me: “Siri, resume my Audible book.” Siri: “Shuffling latest songs from Apple Music.”
There’s no search box because you’re not supposed to type while driving; only I’m not driving — I’m in my kitchen! This shows how much of a CarPlay port the apps are; they haven’t been updated to account for the fact that this device is stationary and in your home. Case in point, when I first pulled up the Apple TV app (the only CarPlay video app currently supported), a warning popped up telling me to make sure I was stationary before watching any video.
Playing audio through CarPlay apps is also buggy. It didn’t always bring up the music control screen, so I had to use my iPhone to control it. Plus, the Audible app often refused to load at all and didn’t work with Siri voice search. Me: “Siri, resume my Audible book.” Siri: “Shuffling latest songs from Apple Music.”
CarPlay support feels like a stopgap, and Apple needs to work with developers to refine the software and add HomeView-specific controls for a better, more integrated experience.
Should you buy a HomeView as a smart speaker?
Much of the confusion around the HomeView stems from treating it like a smart speaker when it’s really a smart display. I get it; I’ve spent the last decade frustrated by smart displays from Google and Amazon that promise a lot but rarely do it all well.
If you don’t care about the other features of a smart display and just want a smart speaker, then the reason to buy a HomeView over a HomePod is if you have a use for it as a touchscreen music controller. This lets anyone in the household easily browse and control what’s playing. Bear in mind, though, Apple Music (with a subscription) is the only app anyone can use to play music on the HomeView, as CarPlay apps require a user profile.
If you want a smart speaker primarily to play music and are happy using your voice or phone to control it, go for a HomePod. If you use Spotify or other third-party music services, consider an Echo Dot or Google Home smart speaker; both let you set a default speaker and a default music provider — such as Spotify.
If you already own HomePods and use Apple Music, the HomeView’s touchscreen will fit in nicely as a simple way to control audio. Just don’t buy one expecting it to fully replace a dedicated smart speaker.

articles.title: Falhas em atualizações e brechas de segurança: o que está por trás dos apagões tecnológicos
articles.text:
Em menos de uma semana, a Microsoft sofreu uma interrupção em massa de serviços, todos os voos nos Estados Unidos ficaram suspensos por horas, os sistemas de comunicação da Agência de Segurança Nacional americana (NSA) apresentaram problemas e os principais bancos do país registraram falhas. Apesar da proximidade temporal, não há evidências de que os incidentes estejam relacionados entre si.
O secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, foi direto: “Não estamos sob um ataque sistêmico. Estes eventos não têm conexão entre si, não estão inter-relacionados.” Ainda assim, a sequência de ocorrências expõe vulnerabilidades do mundo tecnológico e nos faz perguntar o que são ou onde estão essas falhas.
O que aconteceu em cada caso
Boa parte das interrupções teve origem em falhas durante atualizações de sistemas. Uma atualização de rede da Microsoft sobrecarregou servidores, levando ao desligamento deles. No caso da aviação americana, no fim de semana de 14 e 15 de novembro, o problema surgiu durante a substituição de cabos de cobre obsoletos por fibra óptica no sistema de telecomunicações do controle de tráfego aéreo, o que deixou milhares de aviões em terra.
Os problemas no sistema interno de comunicação da NSA e nas plataformas iCloud e Apple Pay também foram atribuídos a falhas ocorridas durante atualizações. Já a interrupção nos pagamentos de bancos americanos foi atribuída a uma “falha de software” do JP Morgan Chase — banco que afirma tratar-se de um incidente de cibersegurança.
Outros casos envolveram vulnerabilidades de segurança identificadas ativamente. A inteligência artificial foi usada para detectar falhas no Java, a terceira linguagem de programação mais popular do mundo, administrada pela Oracle. O pesquisador Scott Helme encontrou código malicioso na plataforma Optimizely, utilizada por algumas das maiores empresas do mundo. Nesse caso, hackers conseguiram roubar cerca de US$ 7 mil (aproximadamente R$ 41 mil) em criptomoedas antes de serem descobertos e expulsos.
O papel da inteligência artificial
“Eu ficaria muito surpreso se todos esses ciberataques e os hackers que os perpetram não estivessem usando inteligência artificial para acelerar o processo”, declarou Scott Helme à rede BBC. A IA tem sido empregada dos dois lados: tanto por quem ataca quanto por quem defende sistemas.
Nos últimos meses, empresas como Anthropic e OpenAI concluíram que é arriscado oferecer ao público em geral acesso aos seus modelos mais avançados antes que determinadas empresas e instituições os utilizem primeiro. Isso permite que profissionais de segurança empreguem a tecnologia para detectar falhas e alertar os demais antes que criminosos tenham acesso — foi o que ocorreu nos casos do Java e do PHP, gerando uma corrida para corrigir as vulnerabilidades antes que pudessem ser exploradas.
Martin Reynolds, diretor de tecnologia de campo da empresa de fornecimento de software Harness, resume o efeito colateral desse processo: “A IA está acelerando a descoberta dos dois lados e agilizando a quantidade de software que é distribuída. Por isso, a quantidade de programas que os desenvolvedores precisam reparar e atualizar está aumentando e o tempo de que eles dispõem para realizar o trabalho está diminuindo.”
Dívida técnica e dependência de poucos provedores
Parte das interrupções é atribuída ao que especialistas chamam de dívida técnica. A expressão é usada quando operadores optam por soluções rápidas para problemas de software em vez de resolver as causas mais profundas. O acúmulo dessas correções superficiais pode gerar dificuldades mais graves ao longo do tempo. A inteligência artificial vem fazendo com que muitas empresas reavaliem sua cibersegurança, o que deve resultar em mais atualizações e, consequentemente, maior potencial de interrupções.
Os episódios também evidenciam a dependência global de um número reduzido de empresas. Microsoft, Amazon e Google gerenciam juntas grande parte dos servidores de informática do planeta. No caso do PHP, o mundo inteiro aguardou enquanto um programador voluntário trabalhava para publicar atualizações aplicáveis. O Java, por sua vez, é utilizado por quase todas as principais empresas do mundo.
“A vulnerabilidade do Oracle Java é um claro lembrete da forte dependência que as empresas têm de um número relativamente pequeno de tecnologias básicas”, afirmou Sheila Pancholi, responsável por garantia de riscos da consultoria britânica RSM UK. “As organizações precisam saber onde residem suas dependências tecnológicas críticas, agir com rapidez quando surgirem vulnerabilidades e comprovar que sua resposta realmente funcionou”, orientou ela.
O engenheiro de segurança Xander Van Raemdonck, da empresa Aikido Security, apontou um obstáculo prático: “O Java é incluído em muitos softwares empresariais e, por isso, muitas empresas não têm uma lista completa de onde ele é executado.” O desafio, segundo ele, é “saber se alguém está exposto”.
O cenário à frente
As ferramentas de IA usadas para encontrar falhas de segurança ainda são recentes e devem continuar identificando vulnerabilidades presentes em códigos há décadas. A Anthropic, entre outras empresas líderes em inteligência artificial, alertou sobre os riscos apresentados pelos seus próprios produtos.
Do lado dos hackers, a assimetria persiste. “Os hackers podem se movimentar com rapidez, sem preocupações e experimentar sem risco de fracasso”, explicou Helme. “Por isso, naturalmente, eles costumam se movimentar um pouco mais rápido. Atualmente, estamos observando uma leve defasagem entre a velocidade dos hackers e a dos defensores.”
As interrupções de serviços têm impacto direto no mundo físico, causando falhas no atendimento médico, no funcionamento de escolas e na capacidade das pessoas de realizarem seu trabalho. Ou, como ocorreu no fim de semana de 14 e 15 de novembro nos Estados Unidos, impedindo aviões de levantar voo.
Beatriz Campos é jornalista formada pela Universidade São Judas Tadeu e jornalista do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Teures NAS? Brauchst du nicht – deine Fritzbox kann das auch
articles.text:
Statt teurem NAS: So nutzt du deine Fritzbox als Netzwerkspeicher
Fritzboxen bieten eine Vielzahl von Features. Einige davon dürften die meisten User:innen gar nicht auf dem Schirm haben. Schließlich ist der Router schnell vergessen, wenn er seine Dienste reibungslos erledigt und Internet in jeden Bereich der Wohnung bringt. Eine dieser oftmals übersehenen Funktionen ist der Netzwerkspeicher der Fritzbox.
Es gibt zwei Wege, um auch von anderen Geräten im Netzwerk auf Dateien zuzugreifen, die per USB-Stick oder Festplatte an die Fritzbox gekoppelt sind. Einziger Nachteil: Die beiden Methoden schließen einander aus. Solltest du etwa den USB-Fernanschluss für die Fritzbox aktiviert haben, funktioniert der Netzwerkspeicher nicht mehr. Was die Unterschiede sind und wie du beide Varianten einrichtest, erfährst du in den jeweiligen Abschnitten.
Fritzbox: So funktioniert der USB-Fernanschluss
Der USB-Fernanschluss ist die einfachste Methode, um die Fritzbox in einen Netzwerkspeicher zu verwandeln. Die Einschränkung dabei ist, dass nicht alle Geräte im Netzwerk auf den USB-Stick oder die Festplatte zugreifen können, die am Router angeschlossen wurde. Beim USB-Fernanschluss stellst du nur die Verbindung zwischen der Fritzbox und einem oder mehreren Windows-Computern her. Wem das reicht, bekommt damit eine schneller umsetzbare Lösung als beim Medienspeicher.
Um den USB-Fernanschluss einzurichten, benötigst du einen PC mit Windows 7 oder höher. Dazu kommt ein passender USB-Stick oder eine Festplatte. Welche Geräte mit deiner Fritzbox kompatibel sind, entnimmst du dabei am besten dem Handbuch, da sich die Spezifikationen von Modell zu Modell unterscheiden können. Hast du den USB-Stick mit dem Router verbunden, kannst du zunächst in deiner Fritzbox-Benutzeroberfläche mit den Vorbereitungen starten.
USB-Fernanschluss in der Fritzbox aktivieren
- Öffne die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox über die Webadresse „fritz.box“ oder über die werksseitig eingestellte IP „192.168.178.1“.
- Klicke in der linken Seitenleiste auf „Heimnetz“ und wähle dort „USB / Speicher“ aus.
- Wähle den Reiter „USB-Einstellungen“ aus.
- Aktiviere am unteren Ende der Seite den Haken bei der Option „USB-Fernanschluss aktiv“.
Windows-PC mit USB-Fernanschluss ausstatten
- Öffne wie oben beschrieben den Bereich „USB-Einstellungen“ in der Fritzbox-Oberfläche.
- Im unteren Bereich findest du einen Download-Button für das Programm „AVM Fritzbox USB-Fernanschluss“.
- Klicke im Anschluss doppelt auf die heruntergeladene Datei, um sie zu installieren.
USB-Fernanschluss unter Windows nutzen
- Klicke im System-Tray von Windows unten rechts auf das kleine USB-Symbol des Fernanschlusses.
- Trage in der Anmeldemaske das Kennwort deiner Fritzbox ein. Solltest du dich bei deiner Fritzbox mit einem Benutzernamen anmelden müssen, trage diesen ebenfalls ein. Andernfalls kann das Feld leer bleiben.
- Wähle „Aktualisieren“ und anschließend per Rechtsklick den angeschlossenen USB-Stick aus.
- Klicke auf „Verbinden“.
Künftig sollte der USB-Speicher, der mit deiner Fritzbox verbunden ist, genauso in Windows angezeigt werden, als wäre er an den PC selbst angeschlossen. Willst du auch mit anderen Windows-Geräten darauf zugreifen, wiederholst du einfach auf den Endgeräten die Installation des Programms und das Verbinden des Sticks.
Fritzbox: So wird der Router zum Netzwerkspeicher
Um den USB-Speicher an der Fritzbox im kompletten Netzwerk nutzen zu können, musst du zunächst, wie oben erwähnt, den USB-Fernanschluss deaktivieren. Der Vorteil im Gegensatz zur ersten Variante ist, dass du auch mit einem Smartphone oder Tablet auf den Speicher zugreifen kannst. Der Zugriff über Windows-PCs ist ebenfalls möglich, genauso wie über andere Betriebssysteme wie macOS.
Fritzbox-Benutzer einrichten
Um die NAS-Funktion an der Fritzbox nutzen zu können, müssen ein Benutzer samt Kennwort festgelegt werden. Das ist zum Glück vergleichsweise schnell erledigt.
- Öffne die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox über die Webadresse „fritz.box“ oder über die werksseitig eingestellte IP „192.168.178.1“.
- Klicke in der linken Seitenleiste auf „System“ und anschließend auf „Fritzbox-Benutzer“.
Du kannst einen vorhandenen Benutzer bearbeiten und bei ihm im Bereich „Berechtigungen“ den Haken bei „Zugang zu NAS-Inhalten“ setzen. Gibt es noch keinen Benutzer oder willst du ein separates Konto für den NAS-Zugang mit eigenem Passwort, kannst du einen neuen Benutzer über den Knopf „Benutzer hinzufügen“ erstellen.
Bei beiden Varianten kannst du nach dem Aktivieren von „Zugang zu NAS-Inhalten“ festlegen, ob der Benutzer vollen Zugriff auf alle Inhalte haben soll oder nur einen Lesezugriff erhält. Über die Option „Individuelle Einstellungen“ und „Zugriffsberechtigung einstellen“ kannst du auch einzelne Ordner für den Zugriff freigeben, während der Rest verwehrt bleibt.
NAS in der Fritzbox aktivieren
- Öffne die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox über die Webadresse „fritz.box“ oder über die werksseitig eingestellte IP „192.168.178.1“.
- Klicke in der Seitenleiste auf „Heimnetz“ und anschließend „USB / Speicher“.
- Wähle im Reiter „Heimnetzfreigabe“ die Option „Zugriff auf Netzlaufwerk (SMB)“ aus.
Darunter kannst du dann einen Namen für den Netzwerkspeicher festlegen, damit du ihn später zuordnen kannst. Zudem siehst du eine Liste aller Benutzer, die NAS-Zugriff haben. So kannst du direkt prüfen, ob das Erstellen aus dem vorherigen Schritt korrekt funktioniert hat. Nach einem letzten Klick auf „Übernehmen“ sind schon alle Voraussetzungen für den Netzwerkspeicher der Fritzbox getroffen. Allerdings gibt es noch Unterschiede bei der Art des Zugriffs.
So kannst du auf deinen Fritzbox-Speicher zugreifen
Mit Geräten, die einen Browser nutzen können, kannst du nach dem Setup über die Adresse „fritz.nas“ auf deinen Netzwerkspeicher zugreifen. Über mobile Geräte wie Smartphones und Tablets kannst du hingegen die Myfritz-App nutzen. Etwas komplizierter ist das Ganze, wenn du über den Datei-Explorer auf Windows-PCs oder über den Finder auf macOS auf den Netzwerkspeicher deiner Fritzbox zugreifen willst.
Unter Windows
- Öffne den Datei-Explorer und gib in der Leiste „\\fritz.box“ ein.
- Gib in der Anmeldemaske die Login-Daten des Benutzers ein, der Zugriff auf den Speicher hat, und aktiviere die Option „Anmeldedaten speichern“.
- Klicke mit der rechten Maustaste auf den Ordner, den du als Netzwerklaufwerk einrichten willst, und wähle „Netzlaufwerk verbinden“ aus.
- Klicke auf „Fertigstellen“.
Unter macOS
- Öffne den Finder und klicke in der Menüleiste auf „Gehe zu“.
- Wähle „Server verbinden“ aus und gib als Adresse „smb:\\fritz.box“ ein.
- Klicke auf „Verbinden“ und gib die Login-Daten des Netzwerknutzers ein.
- Wähle den Ordner aus, der freigegeben werden soll, und klicke im Menü auf „Ablage“, gefolgt von „Alias erzeugen“.
- Ziehe das Alias in den Bereich „Favoriten“ des macOS-Finders.
Die NAS Funktion der Fritzbox ist für kleinere Dateien und ein kleines Archiv ok und als „Billig“ Lösung zu gebrauchen.
Aber aufgrund des Fehlendes Caches und der Geschwindigkeit ist sie Absolut nicht zu gebrauchen, eine Gute NAS Lösung bereitzustellen.
Dazu sollte man dann besser auch bessere Lösungen zurückgreifen.

articles.title: Sabrent Voltik 252W 8-port USB PD 3.0 Charger Quick Look
articles.text:
Sabrent sent us this charger, and while we do not generally review USB chargers, we thought we would take a few photos and share it since it has been pretty useful. The Voltik 252W 8-port USB PD 3.0 Charger is a desktop charging station with four USB-C ports and four USB-A ports, and Sabrent rates it at 252W of total output. That is a lot of power for something that sits on a desk, and the port layout is what makes it worth a closer look.
Here is the unit via an Amazon Affiliate link.
Sabrent Voltik 252W Hardware Overview
The enclosure is a black rectangular block that is not really what we would want from a travel charger, but it works well on a desk.
The front face has a display at the top, then the four USB-C ports, then the four USB-A ports below them. There is also a button for the LCD.
The USB-C ports are arranged in two rows of two. The upper row is labeled C1A and C1B, and the lower row is labeled C2A and C2B. Sabrent rates each USB-C port at up to 100W, which is enough for a laptop on its own. The 252W figure is the station’s combined output, so the four USB-C ports cannot all deliver 100W at the same time. Sabrent lists support for PD 3.0, PPS, QC 4.0, and QC 3.0.
Below the USB-C ports are the four USB-A ports, also in two rows, with the Sabrent logo underneath. Sabrent rates each USB-A port at up to 18W.
Here is a shot of the LCD lit up and showing eight port boxes labeled C1A, C2A, A1A, and A2A across the top and C1B, C2B, A1B, and A2B across the bottom. The screen can cycle through each port to show current wattage, voltage, amperage, and internal temperature by using the button between ports C1A and C1B. Other chargers do that, but if you do not have something like that yet, then it is something that if you read STH, you will like.
The power-input panel has the AC inlet, a printed rating label that includes the model AX-8PTC and the per-port and shared output modes. It is nice that the unit directly takes AC power rather than through an external power brick.
Of course, if you want to use it on the road, it is pretty easy to find a different input cable for this one.
The rear face has two long raised strips along its edges and two rectangular recesses in the center for a mounting plate.
The mounting plate has four fixing holes and two rectangular hooks, shown here with two black fixings in front and the charger behind. That hardware points to mounting the station rather than leaving it loose on the desktop.
Final Words
The Sabrent Voltik 252W is interesting because it consolidates a desk full of chargers into one unit with eight ports and a display that shows the status of each port’s voltage, current, temperature, and time. It is quite useful to know if something is charging, or if it is on, and how fast. On the other hand, we have seen notebooks that draw over 100W via USB Type-C, so even though this is a huge USB charger, it cannot charge everything.
For a desk with several devices that need to charge, that combination of port count, power, and feedback is the practical case for a single station in place of a drawer full of separate adapters. We now have four of these.
Where to Buy
If you want to buy one of these or check the current pricing, here is an Amazon affiliate link.
“even though this is a huge USB charger, it cannot charge everything.”
Sure it can. Just not quite as fast as you’d like. And maybe it’ll lose ground if you’re doing something that pushes your machine to its absolute limits.

articles.title: Assez de Google Messages et de ses fonctionnalités lourdes ? Adoptez l'une de ces alternatives simples pour vos SMS
articles.text:
Google Messages en fait trop : voici 3 alternatives pour envoyer vos SMS
La solution par défaut sur Android pour envoyer des SMS, Google Messages, ne cesse de s'enrichir. Mais à force de vouloir rattraper WhatsApp et autres messageries instantanées, l'application de Google est devenue très lourde et curieuse. Voici des alternatives pour revenir à quelque chose de plus simple et moins dépendant de Google.
Depuis plusieurs mois, Google a clairement pour vocation d'enrichir son application Google Messages à coups de mises à jour. Initialement simple logiciel pour gérer les SMS, Google Messages supporte désormais le protocole RCS et étoffe régulièrement son interface et ses fonctionnalités pour devenir une alternative à WhatsApp, Signal et autres Telegram. Une bonne nouvelle pour ceux qui utilisent beaucoup l'application, mais une mauvaise pour qui n'a pas l'utilité pour autant de lourdeurs, d'espace de stockage occupé et de connexions toujours plus nombreuses à l'ogre Google.
S'il est possible de désactiver des fonctionnalités dans Google Messages pour en simplifier le fonctionnement, l'heure peut également être venue d'aller voir la concurrence. Voici trois alternatives, qui ont toutes un point commun important à relever : elles ne supportent pas le protocole RCS. Il s'agit donc de solutions uniquement capables d'envoyer et de recevoir des SMS et MMS traditionnels.
Et si vous avez des alternatives à partager, direction les commentaires !
Fossify Messages
Démarrons avec la solution la plus épurée : Fossify Messages. Disponible sur le Play Store ou F-Droid, l'application open source a le bon goût d'être totalement gratuite et dépourvue de la moindre publicité. En ne demandant pas l'autorisation d'accès à Internet au smartphone Android, le logiciel permet ainsi des échanges totalement privés et isolés sur l'appareil.
Les fonctionnalités centrales attendues sont là, comme les conversations de groupe, la recherche, le blocage, l'envoi de fichiers, la sauvegarde ou encore l'envoi de messages rapides ou planifiés. Il ne s'agit pas de la solution la plus complète existante, mais les personnes en quête de simplicité trouveront difficilement mieux.
Pulse SMS
Passons à Pulse SMS. A l'opposé de la précédente proposition, cette solution veut être une solution très moderne et donc multiplateformes. L'argument principal de Pulse SMS est de pouvoir retrouver ses messages sur smartphone, tablette, navigateur et même Android TV. Une sauvegarde dans le cloud et le chiffrement de bout-en-bout sont aussi de la partie.
Sans surprise, pour ces fonctionnalités et bien d'autres (thèmes par conversation, réactions, recherche, planification, dossiers et sécurisation des échanges...), il faudra accepter de créer un compte et possiblement de craquer pour un compte Premium.
Textra SMS
Terminons avec Textra SMS. Idéale pour les amateurs de Material Design et de la possibilité d'adopter de multiples couleurs pour chaque contact, l'application se veut spécialement rapide et minimaliste malgré ses très nombreuses options de personnalisation et fonctionnalités (réactions, envoi retardé, planification, mémos vocaux...).
On relèvera cependant la nécessité d'avoir un compte pour utiliser Textra SMS, tandis que pour supprimer la présence de publicité il faudra un compte Premium. Ce dernier a au moins le mérite d'être accessible après un paiement unique de 15 $.
Suivez toute l'actualité des Numériques sur Google Actualités et sur la chaîne WhatsApp des Numériques

articles.title: FBI Investigating Apparent Hack of Its Key National Criminal Justice Database, AP Source Says
articles.text:
The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of a national law enforcement database that it maintains, a person familiar with the matter said Saturday.
The National Crime Information Center, known as the NCIC, is a computerized database of criminal justice information that is available to local, state and federal law enforcement agencies and includes records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history data, stolen property and other topics.
The FBI declined to comment Saturday on the apparent hack, which was first reported by CNN and confirmed to The Associated Press by a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak by name and spoke on the condition of anonymity.
The scope of the problem was not immediately clear.
Asked about the subject on Saturday, President Donald Trump said in a Fox News Channel interview: “We just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good.”
News that the NCIC was targeted comes as the country has encountered a series of digital outages in the government and private sector that Trump administration officials have said were caused by routine efforts to upgrade computer systems and fix vulnerabilities, rather than a cyberattack. There was no immediate indication that the FBI incident was related to those outages.
The bureau has historically been a frequent target for hackers.
In September, for instance, a criminal hacking group known as ShinyHunters revealed that it had obtained a massive trove of data on FBI employees and applicants and had compromised the bureau’s jobs portal.
And in March, the FBI disclosed that it was investigating “suspicious activities” on an internal system that contains sensitive information related to surveillance operations and investigations.
Related: Ransomware Response Expert Arrested in ShinyHunters FBI Hack Probe
Related: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Hack, Demands Retraction of Threat Report

articles.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
articles.text:
This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the vibe-hacking of everything, follow David Pierce. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.
The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
Large language models can now redesign your TV and upgrade your camera for you. Is the physical world ready to be Claude Code-d?
How it started
Like so many things with AI, it’s not that large language models opened up some wholly new capability. For as long as there have been gadgets, a few users have been hacking, modding, jailbreaking, and tweaking them to their liking. What is new is that it’s easy now. People all over the world are discovering that they can use large language models to hack their hardware simply by prompting Claude Code or Codex to do it. It has led to a boom in developer-friendly gadgets and created a market for better software on just about every device you can think of.
For one developer in India who goes by Gathin T, the whole thing started almost on a whim. “One afternoon, I was fiddling with my TV, and it was just really shitty,” he tells me. His was a set made by Xiaomi and running Android TV, with so many ads and so much interface chaos it was hard to even change inputs. And he got to thinking: If you can install another launcher on your Android phone, maybe you can do the same to your TV. “The first thing that came to mind was to remove the bloatware from the TV,” he says. “Then I thought, why not make it look better?”
Gathin prompted Claude Code and discovered that with a couple of permissions tweaks and a toggle of USB debugging mode, his chatbot could control his TV as long as they were on the same Wi-Fi network. An hour and a half later, Gathin had redesigned his TV to his liking — no more onscreen ads, a simpler interface, easier access to his PlayStation on another input. He posted on X about what he’d done and promptly went viral. So Gathin put together his work, bought a domain, and launched CleanYourTV as a tool for helping other people solve their own television interfaces. It became one of the most popular repositories on GitHub, got thousands of pull requests and feature ideas, and inspired countless people to point their own chatbot at their big screen.
Gathin is careful to note that the only TVs that work this easily are based on Android. (He has Claude Code-d his way through other operating systems, but those involve more explicit jailbreaking and rooting, so he’s more reluctant to share the process so widely.) But for vibe hackers everywhere, the good news is that Android kind of runs everything. From dishwashers to digital photo frames to luxury cars, even gadgets that don’t look like Android often run Android. Even when they don’t, odds are good that there’s another way in. If there’s a hidden API, your LLM can find it. If the firmware file lives on a website somewhere, your LLM can unpack it, explore it, and repackage it to your liking.
Again, few of the technical capabilities here are new, and enterprising developers have been doing this kind of work for many years. Some have even been using AI for several years to make the work easier. But when Claude Code first had its “oh my gosh it works” moment in late 2025, developers began leaning on the tools even more — and non-developers began discovering they, too, could build software now. And over the course of 2026, more and more people began pointing that capability at their hardware.
How it’s going
Now, it seems, all hardware is hacker hardware. Camera enthusiasts embraced the possibilities of vibe hacking as fast as anyone, using LLMs to repackage their camera software in all sorts of ways. Firmware hacks like Magic Lantern are a staple of the camera community, but suddenly it seems like everyone is using AI to add new recording capabilities, support higher resolutions, or even add new looks and color profiles to their shots. Many are using the tools to give their old gear new life; other, more enterprising vibe coders are pointing their bots at their brand-new hardware.
The music world is being similarly upended. Budding musicians are turning cheap synths into powerful new kinds of gear, and a cheap gadget known as the M-Vave FM-1 has become a popular target for custom firmware and new features. M-Vave has even released an open-source firmware, embracing the hackers as other companies have tried to keep them out. The FM-1 is cheap, it’s easy to hack, and it’s raising questions about what higher-end manufacturers can even do to compete.
Gamers, who are also using AI to decompile and mod the games they love, are using LLMs to add new features to their consoles. One vibe coder found a way to play PlayStation 2 discs on a PlayStation 5; lots of gamers have built scripts that allow them to use their favorite controllers on other devices.
In the games world in particular, this has caused the industry to fight back. Game makers are looking for ways to protect their work from being decompiled and made available for free and on other platforms. Luke Dicken, a longtime gaming executive who was recently Take-Two’s head of artificial intelligence, recently predicted to Kotakuthat the industry will start to embrace “more invasive DRM, platform-level solutions, and probably more of a push towards streaming solutions since nobody can decompile what they can’t get their hands on.” Hardware makers will push harder to lock down their systems; companies across the board will pursue legal action to protect their intellectual property.
All this hardware access also creates new risks for users. When you install a vibe-coded version of your camera’s firmware, you are now well outside the bounds of what the camera manufacturer is equipped to help you solve. You might be stuck asking Claude to fix the problems Claude created. As Ritchie Roesch wrote recently at Fuji X Weekly, “It’s not so much if someone’s camera will become a permanent paperweight, it’s a matter of when and how many, and whether it will be yours.”
The safer (and less litigious) route for the enterprising vibe hacker lies in an entirely new kind of hardware. ESP32 modules, which package networking chips, microphones, speakers, and more into a simple and hacker-friendly package, are suddenly everywhere in hardware communities. (Think Raspberry Pis, but even cheaper and more versatile.) So sure, you can use Claude Code to jailbreak and de-Amazon your Kindle, but why do that when you can buy a device like the M5Stack PaperMono, an ESP32-based e-paper device you can make into whatever you want?
ESP32 modules are perfectly suited to help you build the kind of hyper-specific device Apple or Samsung would never consider. With a few dollars and a few prompts, you can build a way to see real-time sea conditions, rig up a monitor for your whole DJ system, or just play Metal Gear Solidon the go. You can even have a dedicated device for your family’s shopping list.
What happens next
The arms race between device manufacturers and vibe hackers is only going to continue. As AI models get more powerful, and both the tools and their users get more sophisticated, it’ll be easier and easier for anyone to point their bot at their TV, their car, or their washing machine and see what happens. Some manufacturers will try their best to keep the hackers out; others will look for ways to safely embrace them. Some users will find incredible new functionality for their tech; others will find they’ve created extraordinarily large and expensive paperweights.
Before long, we’re going to see a lot of ESP32 devices turned into more consumer-friendly hardware. Meta is already leading the charge with its Muse Charm and the Muse Gadgets program, through which you can either buy a nicely packaged ESP32 module or use your own to quickly spin up a dedicated AI device. This kind of gadget — just a simple computing module in a pretty box — is going to be everywhere.
At the same time, we’re already seeing some vibe hackers turn into proper software vendors. Gathin, for instance, has spent a lot of time reckoning with the responsibility he feels for what happens when people use CleanYourTV to hack their televisions. He’s tweaked the prompts he shares to first take a backup of your TV’s software in order to make it easy to restore if something goes wrong, and to make note of every change it makes along the way. The CleanYourTV system also checks its progress as it goes and spins up agents to manually test if something has gone wrong, and Gathin hopes it’s increasingly foolproof.
But it’s not foolproof. It might never be. Devices change all the time; every software update introduces new possibilities and new problems. So Gathin recommends the same thing I hear from vibe coders and vibe hackers all the time: Never give the bots access to something you can’t afford to lose. “Even for fiddling with stuff,” he says, “I have an external computer which runs through Linux. So I just use it like a sandbox environment to test things out.” If you’re going to try and vibe-hack your phone (which lots of people are doing) or your computer (which lots of people are also doing), do it carefully. And make lots of backups.
By the way
- If you are vibe-hacking an existing gadget, you are practically always voiding your warranty. There are no guarantees, and you definitely can’t count on customer support to get you out of a jam or offer you a refund.
- You can buy ESP32 devices from lots of places, but a lot of folks recommend starting on Waveshare, which has a big selection and pretty good prices.
- Espressif, which created the ESP chip, also recently launched its own development system, called ESP-Claw. It’s designed to make programming your ESP device even simpler.
- Raspberry Pis are also good vibe-hacking devices! You can even run Claude Code on a Raspberry Pi… to hack a Raspberry Pi.
Read this
- Check out Terrence O’Brien’s deeper look at the AI vibe-hacking world, and the ways in which these new synths — in particular the FM-1 — are changing the way people think about music gear.
- Elektor has a good piece about the history and technical details of ESP32, which goes back more than a decade.
- Richie at Fuji X Weekly posted a follow-up to that original blog about vibe-coded firmware, diving into both the debate about AI in general and about what it even means to use a particular camera. “If that camera can be hacked with AI vibe coded 3rd party firmware to change its functions and features, is it still the same camera?”
- Just as AI is being used to revive and improve old gadgets, The Verge’s Andrew Webster found that so too are old games being reimagined with AI. For better and for worse.
- I wrote a while back about the personal software revolution and how vibe coding meant everyone could build the exact software they want. The same thing is coming fast to hardware everywhere.

Futebol ao vivo: conheça aplicativos para assistir aos jogos pelo celular
Futebol é uma paixão nacional. Por isso, nada mais natural do que ver a internet popularizando o acesso aos campeonatos nacionais e internacionais no Brasil. Com as mudanças da tecnologia, ficou bastante fácil assistir a jogos de futebol ao vivo e online no seu celular.
Filmes e séries, por exemplo, já podem ser assistidos a qualquer hora e em qualquer lugar, graças aos serviços de streaming. Mas não são apenas essas produções que podem se beneficiar das ferramentas modernas: os esportes também. Assim, já é bastante fácil assistir a jogos de futebol ao vivo e online, seja do seu celular ou do computador.
O Olhar Digital preparou um artigo especial ensinando como fazer para acompanhar os principais campeonatos de futebol — nacionais e internacionais, de clubes ou seleções — diretamente do celular ou computador via streaming ao vivo!
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.
